azd env set AZURE_PRINCIPAL_TYPE <User-or-ServicePrincipal>

Use the identity's object ID, not its client ID. Detection failures report the required inputs. Explicit identity inputs do not authenticate the process; keep credentials out of checked-in files.

Separate environment, resource-group, identity, data and configuration boundaries by stage. Set the resource group destinations before first provision. Preserve existing mappings on retries.

docs.title: Step 3: Prepare remote state outside the workload
docs.text:
An existing Azure Storage account and blob container are required. The workload does not create or bootstrap them. Keep the backend outside every workload resource group and outside the workload's Terraform-managed resources. It must remain available after azd down.

The authorized executor needs Reader on the storage account for metadata lookup and Storage Blob Data Contributor on the state container. The backend uses Microsoft Entra ID (AzureAD) Blob authentication. Arrange network access from each deployment runner, restricted access, retention or backups, and an owner-reviewed recovery process.

Configure the selected azd environment:

azd env set TF_STATE_RESOURCE_GROUP <state-resource-group>
azd env set TF_STATE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT <state-storage-account>
azd env set TF_STATE_CONTAINER <state-container>

TF_STATE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID defaults to AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID. For a backend in a different subscription, also set:

azd env set TF_STATE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID <state-subscription-id>

The state key is agent-landing-zone/${AZURE_ENV_NAME}.tfstate, giving each environment its own blob. azd renders infra/terraform/provider.conf.json from these settings, including the canonical ARM_ENVIRONMENT. Confirm the cloud, account, container and environment name before provisioning; keep .azure/ metadata private. See the official remote-state guidance and Azure Storage backend reference.

docs.title: State protection
docs.text:
azd 1.37.1 passes -lock=false to Terraform plan and apply, so these operations do not acquire the Azure Blob lease used for native state protection. Use the execution and access controls below; they do not enable backend locking.

  • Individual environments: local azd may operate the configured remote backend. Do not overlap writers to the same state.
  • Shared and production environments: allow one authorized writer/executor, normally a pipeline. Restrict state write access to that executor and queue all operations without canceling an active run.
  • Serialize by actual state identity: cloud, backend subscription, storage account, container and resolved state key. Branch-scoped concurrency and cancel-in-progress are insufficient. No other branch, checkout, terminal or pipeline may write the same state concurrently.
  • Keep workspaces separate: each active environment operation needs its own checkout/workspace so generated inputs are not overwritten.

docs.title: Private deployment records
docs.text:
Before persisting backend settings, the adapter creates .azure/<environment-name>/terraform-backend.json on first use and verifies it on subsequent runs. This immutable, nonsecret record binds the backend subscription, resource group, account, container, resolved key and cloud. Keep it private with the environment metadata.

Retain the original resource-groups.json, terraform-resource-groups.json and application/environment bindings from that same directory. They record destinations and Terraform group ownership. Restore these original records on a clean runner before refresh, provisioning or teardown. Output refresh does not reconstruct them; missing or changed bindings block the operation.

docs.title: Step 4: Choose the application and foundation inputs
docs.text:
Even an infrastructure-only deployment binds to an application definition. Choose the application, topology and ingestion intent before first provision; one environment binds to one application ID. For a custom definition, follow Bring your own app and set:

azd env set AGENTLZ_APP_DEFINITION <path-to-app-definition.json>

For the supplied Agent Application, the default is hosted-no-panel, with maf_lite, Foundry IQ and no Agent App Ingestion. It still needs the approved HOSTED_AGENT_RESOURCE_SCOPE before service configuration. Review the application and identity choices and configure per-user document authorization before deploying the application.

Use private networking for production or sensitive data:

azd env set NETWORK_ISOLATION true

Plan standalone or hub integration, existing VNet/DNS ownership, permitted egress, models, optional resources and regions using Deployment choices and Deployment settings. Public endpoints are only for approved, short-lived evaluations without sensitive data. Do not weaken isolation to recover a failure.

Use documented azd env set inputs and the root main.parameters.json for structured values. Keep JSON booleans, numbers, arrays and objects in their native types. For example, an empty public IP allowlist is the existing parameters.allowedIpRanges.value entry set to [].

Preprovision validates the provider/application binding, resolves the shared topology and runs a typed adapter to generate infra/terraform/main.tfvars.json. This file is ignored by Git and regenerated; do not edit it. For Terraform, infra/main.parameters.json is a shared preflight diagnostic artifact, not the Terraform deployment input. Also leave generated .azure/ files to azd.

When a managed jumpbox is enabled and no password is supplied, Terraform owns the persistent generated password. Treat state and generated inputs as sensitive; the hooks do not generate a fresh password on each run.

docs.title: Step 5: Review and provision
docs.text:
Confirm the selected environment, source revision, provider/path, backend key, destination groups, approved inputs, quota and permissions before applying. Review the resolved resources, network exposure, routes and role changes. The read-only application egress report is:

python -m config.deployment.egress --plan --environment <environment-name>

This report covers application egress only; it is not a Terraform infrastructure preview. Obtain approval for the infrastructure changes before provisioning.

After the backend, inputs and infrastructure changes are approved:

azd provision

azd invokes Terraform and the shared pre/post-provision hooks. Provisioning creates the foundation, reconciles access and configures services; it does not build or publish application images or create a running hosted agent version. Selected Container Apps may initially have placeholder images. Reprovisioning must not restore placeholders over deployed application images.

All flat Terraform outputs flow natively into azd and are consumed by the shared postprovision and predeploy hooks. No manual output copying is needed. Terraform publishes foundation-owned App Configuration connections, model metadata and declared additional settings. Shared postprovision seeds only missing defaults; the runtime publisher updates its explicitly owned keys. See configuration ownership. The shared platform output reference explains AGENTLZ_PLATFORM_OUTPUTS and flat keys published in App Configuration under label agent-lz. The platform document is not the full azd output set.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
1. Confirm Terraform and every required configuration step succeeded. Record failures as incomplete even if an outer command returned success.
  2. Inventory every destination group and compare new and reused resources with the approved inputs. Verify private endpoints in their actual groups.
  3. Check backend access and state-key isolation without printing state or secrets. Confirm that resources and state refer to this environment.

  4. Read the expected platform output from the actual configuration store:

    az appconfig kv show --endpoint <app-configuration-endpoint> \
  --key AGENTLZ_PLATFORM_OUTPUTS --label agent-lz --auth-mode login

  5. From the intended runner, verify private DNS, TLS reachability, approved private-link connections and service data-plane roles. Do not expose public endpoints to bypass a failed check.

  6. Confirm no application image build or publication occurred. A placeholder response is not evidence that application sign-in or retrieval works.

Keep the source revision, manifest, provider lock file, nonsecret inputs and validation results. Protect state, plans, generated inputs, logs and .azure/.

docs.title: Complete deferred private configuration
docs.text:
If provisioning explicitly deferred service configuration while a connected host was prepared, keep the same source, provider/path, application binding, destination mapping, inputs and remote backend on that host. Securely restore the original deployment records, selected environment/application bindings and the exact reviewed parameter declaration, including any required private declaration. Keep the same backend and cloud. azd env refresh does not restore those records or declared intent. Missing required declarations fail rather than being reconstructed from defaults, outputs or state. After restoring the environment, complete configuration:

azd env set RUN_FROM_JUMPBOX true
azd env set AZURE_SKIP_NETWORK_ISOLATION_WARNING false
azd hooks run postprovision

Verify platform outputs and data-plane readiness before deploying applications. Do not bypass private-link approval or protected-retrieval gates.

docs.title: Reconfigure or recover the foundation
docs.text:
Keep the same provider and remote state. Back up required data and configuration, preserve names, regions, application layout and group mappings, and review proposed changes before re-running azd provision. Use the coordinated product source, committed provider lock and reviewed module versions for each update.

After a failure or interrupted run, pause the queue and confirm the executor and its Terraform operation have stopped before starting any replacement. Inspect actual resources and remote state, then recover or retry through the same authorized executor. Do not use a parallel manual session for recovery. If executor authority must move, revoke the former writer's access and confirm it has stopped before authorizing its replacement.

Restore state only under an owner-reviewed recovery plan consistent with actual resources, with other writes stopped. Reverting code does not restore data or guarantee rollback. Preserve state, resource names and security settings during recovery.

Every direct and transitive provider version is pinned exactly, with Windows/Linux checksums in infra/terraform/.terraform.lock.hcl. Native azd initialization uses -upgrade; the exact pins constrain provider selection. Read-only lock-file validation runs separately in CI, not as an inline azd option. Review provider and module updates deliberately.

docs.title: Add the application later
docs.text: With the same configured foundation and bound application, continue at Deploy the application. azd deploy consumes the manifest pins and outputs; another provision is not required merely to prepare the hosted image.

docs.title: Remove the foundation
docs.text:
Removal is destructive and needs separate authorization. Inventory every destination and dependent application, back up retained data, and review Terraform ownership and the deletion scope, including reused resources and hub/DNS attachments. Do not infer safety from a resource-group name or tag.

Use the same product root, Terraform configuration and selected environment. The guard verifies the original common group binding, terraform-resource-groups.json and terraform-backend.json. Missing records or changes to the provider, groups or backend address block teardown.

Native azd delegates to Terraform state-scoped destroy, including owned and bring-your-own split-group layouts. The hook does not issue imperative resource-group deletion. Review the plan and all Terraform-owned groups: owning a group can put its contents within the destruction boundary. Bring-your-own groups retain their recorded lookup-only ownership.

At the verified azd 1.37.1, review without deletion:

azd down --no-prompt

Without --force, that Terraform command previews and skips deletion. After separate deletion approval, interactive azd down requests confirmation. Automation can use azd down --force only to explicitly authorize destruction, through the same single-writer queue. Do not use force or purge as a repair shortcut or bypass a failed binding check.

The backend storage, container, permissions and recovery data must remain outside workload teardown and available throughout recovery. Retiring that backend is a separate owner-approved operation after workload retirement and retention review. Preserve shared hub, DNS, monitoring and other reused resources.

docs.title: Embed chat
docs.text:
Agent App UI provides a floating Chainlit Copilot widget for an existing portal. Its script renders in an open Shadow DOM, a separate part of the portal page's document structure, not an iframe containing another web page.

This is Agent App UI embedding, not Copilot Studio. The UI remains in Container Apps, with the orchestrator hosted in Foundry and grounding through Foundry IQ. The pinned UI embedding reference contains the component integration contract.

This page describes requirements, not a turnkey portal integration. Portal token acquisition, Content Security Policy (CSP) and widget lifecycle require application work. Infrastructure deployment and component reloads follow the Deploy full stack runbook.

docs.title: UI and portal contract
docs.text:
The portal has its own Entra client registration and acquires a delegated v2 access token for the UI API. The API exposes user_impersonation; an ID token or Graph token is not valid. The portal's delegated API permissions and consent are separate from the UI's server-side Foundry OBO exchange. Agent Application access explains that downstream path.

UI runtime setting Entra embedding contract CHAINLIT_COPILOT_ENABLED true enables embedding; default is disabled. CHAINLIT_COPILOT_AUTH_MODE entra. CHAINLIT_URL Canonical UI HTTPS origin, for example https://chat.contoso.com. CHAINLIT_ALLOWED_ORIGINS Exact distinct portal HTTPS origins, for example https://portal.contoso.com. CHAINLIT_COPILOT_ENTRA_TENANT_ID Issuing Entra tenant's unique ID. CHAINLIT_COPILOT_ENTRA_AUDIENCE Expected UI API access-token aud. CHAINLIT_COPILOT_ENTRA_REQUIRED_SCOPE Scope name, normally user_impersonation.

Origins contain only scheme, host and optional port, without wildcard, null, credentials, path, query or fragment. CHAINLIT_ROOT_PATH must be empty. The validator accepts the configured tenant and v2 issuer only. For v2 tokens, aud is normally the API's application client ID, while the requested scope uses the API's fully qualified URI. Access token claims describes the distinction.

These are UI runtime settings, normally under App Configuration label agent-lz, not azd deployment inputs. Nonempty process environment values override embedding settings. The UI loads them at startup. Deployment settings identifies their configuration boundary. The existing session-signing secret stays protected.

The widget requires one Uvicorn process, one active Container Apps revision and exactly one replica because sessions and rate limits are process-local. Same-site HTTPS subdomains work with the default CHAINLIT_COOKIE_SAMESITE=lax. Cross-site portals require none, with Secure and HttpOnly cookies, but browser third-party-cookie policy can still prevent a session. A standalone UI link remains available if browser cookie policy blocks embedding.

docs.title: Browser and gateway boundaries
docs.text:
The portal CSP must permit scripts from the controlled UI origin and HTTPS and secure WebSocket (WSS) connections to it. The bundle runs with the portal page's JavaScript privileges; Shadow DOM does not isolate security.

It also injects inline styles, which can conflict with the portal's CSP. A compatible policy retains the portal's nonce/hash protections rather than broadly enabling unsafe-inline. Embedding does not require weakening frame-ancestors or X-Frame-Options.

The gateway contract preserves the external UI origin, cookies, browser Origin, and WebSocket upgrades. Required paths include /copilot/index.js, /copilot/auth/bootstrap, /copilot/auth/logout, /project/settings, /copilot/auth/recovery, /public/protected-auth-recovery.js, /ws/socket.io polling/upgrades and /api/download/{grant_token}. Container Apps ingress supports WebSockets. Browsers still need authorized network access to private UI ingress; embedding does not make it public.

The origin allow-list constrains browsers, not arbitrary HTTP clients that can forge Origin. Entra validation and network/gateway authorization remain necessary.

docs.title: Session lifecycle
docs.text:
The portal's Microsoft Authentication Library (MSAL) integration acquires the UI API token in memory. A credentialed POST /copilot/auth/bootstrap carries it in the bearer header before the widget mounts. Bootstrap validates token and user admission, then creates an opaque server-side session cookie. The token is not a widget accessToken and does not belong in a URL, local storage or portal source.

The embedded session retains the delegated token server-side for the hosted client's OBO exchange. HOSTED_AGENT_AUTH_MODE=user_delegated preserves that caller boundary. Protected document access still requires the hosted retrieval integration; the bundled UI uses the same Search OBO path as standalone chat. Bootstrap alone does not establish downstream consent or source permissions.

Use the bundled recovery helper rather than implementing a claims handshake. After authenticated bootstrap, load it with credentials and install it against the portal's existing MSAL account and UI API scopes:

const helper = document.createElement("script");
helper.src = `${chainlitServer}/public/protected-auth-recovery.js`;
helper.crossOrigin = "use-credentials";
await new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
  helper.onload = resolve;
  helper.onerror = reject;
  document.head.appendChild(helper);
});
const stopRecovery = window.installProtectedAuthRecovery({
  msalInstance,
  account: signedInAccount,
  tenantId: configuredTenantId,
  scopes: configuredUiApiScopes,
  chainlitServer,
  statusElement: document.getElementById("agent-lz-status"),
  widgetConfig: { theme: "light" },
});

Provide the agent-lz-status status element. MSAL must use memoryStorage for both its regular and temporary caches, storeAuthStateInCookie: false, and no PII logging. The selected account must remain active. Tenant and scopes come from portal configuration, never the challenge or widget.

The helper handles the named recovery notification, fetches validated claims through authenticated POST /copilot/auth/recovery, and displays an explicit portal sign-in button. After MSAL verification, it completes recovery with the fresh UI token and remounts the widget without sending a message. Recovery tickets expire after 180 seconds. Ordinary source denials do not start this interaction. Do not send embedded users through standalone OAuth or replay failed turns. Call stopRecovery() before the logout/account-switch sequence below. Keep tokens and claims out of URLs, local storage and portal logs.

Native citation downloads use authenticated principal/session-bound selectors and recheck source access on each click. Shared Blob/ADLS downloads also need Storage delegated consent and user source permissions. See protected citation downloads. Anonymous sessions cannot redeem these selectors.

Session lifetime ends at the earlier of token expiry and CHAINLIT_COPILOT_SESSION_TTL_SECONDS (default 3600 seconds). It has no silent standalone OAuth refresh. Logout/account switching requires widget unmount, local thread-state cleanup and credentialed POST /copilot/auth/logout before another account's bootstrap. Restart, revision switch and eviction invalidate the process-local session and download-grant state.

docs.title: Integration evidence
docs.text:
Successful bootstrap and cookie acceptance allow /project/settings and the chat socket to authenticate. Invalid/expired tokens return 401; disallowed origins return 403. Expiry can also surface as WebSocket 4401 or Socket.IO authentication failure. Bootstrap throttling returns 429 with Retry-After; authoritative rate limits need gateway enforcement.

An integration is incomplete without account-switch, logout, cookie-policy and two-user document allow/deny tests. Do not work around token failures with anonymous fallback or service-identity retrieval.

docs.title: Disabling embedding
docs.text: The portal widget and CHAINLIT_COPILOT_ENABLED control different sides of the integration. Disabling the UI setting takes effect after a UI process reload. It does not remove standalone chat or alter the hosted agent.

docs.title: Unsupported edges
docs.text:
• Iframes, same-origin subpaths and multi-process/multi-replica embedded sessions are unsupported by this widget integration.
  • Anonymous embedding supplies no user token and cannot call the default user-delegated hosted path. It disables durable threads, uploads and private citation downloads; its endpoint is independent of portal login.
  • Upload controls require the separately deployed ingestion capability. Embedding does not add native hosted-agent uploads.

A separately authenticated client is an application extension under Bring your own app.

docs.title: Fabric IQ
docs.text:
Fabric grounding queries data where it lives rather than ingesting a copy into a landing-zone index. A Fabric data agent answers analytical questions over its configured data, including Power BI semantic models. A Fabric IQ ontology binds business entities and relationships to data.

This page explains the integrated native knowledge-source options and their authorization requirements. Deployment procedures are in the Deploy full stack runbook.

docs.title: Data agents and ontologies are different sources
docs.text:
Foundry IQ source Fabric object fabricDataAgent A published data agent, identified by workspace ID and data agent item ID. fabricOntology An ontology, identified by workspace ID and ontology item ID.

A semantic model ID is neither a data agent ID nor an ontology ID. These remote sources query Fabric at retrieval time and do not need Agent App Ingestion. Both knowledge-source integrations are preview. Microsoft documents data agent sources and ontology sources separately.

docs.title: Fabric access and governance
docs.text:
A data agent needs a supported capacity, tenant settings, configured data sources and publication. Consumers need access to both the agent and its underlying data. For the semantic-model data-agent path, Microsoft specifies Read permission on the model; Build permission is not required for that interaction. Authoring permissions are separate. The Fabric data agent guide describes the Fabric-side procedure.

Search and the Fabric workspace must share an Entra tenant. Data permissions, model row-level security and regional data-handling requirements still apply. Private Azure networking does not configure Fabric workspace networking. Preview and cross-service data movement require governance review.

docs.title: What the accelerator registers
docs.text:
FABRIC_DATA_AGENT_ENABLED, FABRIC_DATA_AGENT_KNOWLEDGE_SOURCE_NAME, FABRIC_DATA_AGENT_WORKSPACE_ID and FABRIC_DATA_AGENT_DATA_AGENT_ID describe data-agent source registration. The separate ontology inputs are FABRIC_IQ_ENABLED, FABRIC_IQ_KNOWLEDGE_SOURCE_NAME, FABRIC_IQ_WORKSPACE_ID and FABRIC_IQ_ONTOLOGY_ID.

The Deployment settings register sources and knowledge-base references in Search. They do not create Fabric items or grant model access. The integrated UI obtains the user's delegated Search token; the hosted runtime forwards it to Search for source authorization. Enabling a source requires its configured knowledge-base binding; a missing binding fails provisioning instead of silently omitting that source. Provisioning can overwrite manual edits to platform-owned objects.

docs.title: Integrated hosted retrieval
docs.text:
The built-in hosted maf_lite path supports native Fabric sources without customer-written identity or response-parsing code. Configure the source and its administrator prerequisites, including FOUNDRY_IQ_API_VERSION=2026-08-01-preview:

Boundary Integrated behavior Delegated identity The UI obtains a separate Search-audience token from the authenticated user's assertion. The hosted connector forwards the raw token in x-ms-query-source-authorization; its workload token authenticates only Search transport. Fabric user permissions and consent still apply. Retrieval reasoning Fabric sources require low or medium. Enabling a bound Fabric source configures low reasoning and the configured planning model; Blob-only retrieval retains minimal. Response parsing The connector reads sourceData.fabricAnswer and textual fabricEmbeddedResources, preserving the Fabric source identity in grounding and citations. API compatibility Fabric source setup and retrieval require the explicit 2026-08-01-preview contract. The default Blob API is not silently changed.

The official data-agent source contract defines the token audience and response fields. Missing delegation, incompatible API settings or source failures stop required retrieval; the connector does not retry without the user credential or substitute application-only access.

An ontology remains a separate source contract, not a substitute data-agent identifier. It uses the same explicit API, reasoning and delegated Search route. Foundry IQ explains how knowledge bases relate to Foundry Agent Service tools; Application access describes sign-in, consent and authentication recovery.

Tokens remain server-side, outside prompts and user-supplied tool arguments. Authorization comes from validated caller context, not model-provided user IDs or group lists.

docs.title: Acceptance and recovery
docs.text:
A known-answer query must first succeed in the published Fabric agent as the intended consumer. End-to-end acceptance then includes the correct source reference, expected analytical result and any returned structured resources. It also includes a user denied model access, users with different row-level security and a missing-token test.

Broader managed-identity grants cannot repair missing delegation. Recovery restores the previous application and settings, removes only the pilot source reference and retains Fabric items or Search objects still used elsewhere. Approved application changes start a new hosted version through the Deploy full stack runbook.

docs.title: Foundry IQ
docs.text:
A knowledge source describes searchable content. A knowledge base binds one or more sources and controls retrieval. Foundry Agent Service can call that knowledge base as a native tool, so the agent can ground answers in retrieved content and return source references.

This page describes Foundry IQ and the Agent Application's integration limits. Deployment follows the Deploy full stack runbook.

docs.title: Managed and remote sources
docs.text:
Indexed sources copy content into Search for retrieval. Remote sources query their service at request time, without copying the source corpus into a local index. Both can return content to the agent and model.

The accelerator defaults to a native Blob source, container documents, standard content extraction and ingestion permission options ["rbacScope"]. Search manages the generated indexing assets. Optional Agent App Ingestion is disabled by default for new environments and is not needed for this source. Ingestion explains native source ingestion, conversation uploads and custom processing.

An existing Search index can be registered as a searchIndex knowledge source. The pipeline that owns that index remains responsible for its content, schema and permission metadata. Registering it does not populate or authorize it. Microsoft documents Blob sources and Search index sources separately.

SharePoint, Work IQ and Fabric IQ describe additional native sources, including previews, and the work needed to integrate them with Agent Application.

docs.title: Native tools and the accelerator boundary
docs.text:
Microsoft's Foundry Agent Service connection guide connects a knowledge base through its MCP endpoint and a Foundry RemoteTool project connection. The connection belongs to the agent's native tool definition.

The accelerator also provisions a Microsoft Entra ID-authenticated CognitiveSearch project connection and publishes KNOWLEDGE_BASE_CONNECTION_ID. The shipped retrieval connector does not consume that ID. It calls the Search endpoint and knowledge base name directly. A provisioned connection alone does not attach a native tool or establish user delegation in the hosted application. A CognitiveSearch connection is not the RemoteTool connection in the native-tool procedure.

The relevant Deployment settings describe distinct objects. The connector reads runtime values from App Configuration with label agent-lz.

Setting Meaning in the shipped connector RETRIEVAL_BACKEND foundry_iq selects knowledge-base retrieval in this connector; it does not attach a native agent tool. RETRIEVAL_AUTH_MODE native_search carries the separately delegated Search credential into native permission enforcement. KNOWLEDGE_BASE_ENDPOINT Search service root, such as https://<service>.search.windows.net, not a Foundry project or retrieve URL. KNOWLEDGE_BASE_NAME Knowledge-base object name, not an index name. FOUNDRY_IQ_KNOWLEDGE_SOURCE_NAME Primary registered source name. FOUNDRY_IQ_PATTERN and FOUNDRY_IQ_KNOWLEDGE_SOURCE_KIND azureBlob for the default source, or matching searchIndex for an existing index. FOUNDRY_IQ_API_VERSION The source and connector contract defaults to 2026-05-01-preview. KNOWLEDGE_BASE_CONNECTION_ID Provisioned project connection metadata, not a connector target selector.

Current Microsoft source examples use contracts beyond the accelerator's default API. Adopting a source requires compatibility across registration, retrieve requests and response parsing, not an API-version edit alone.

docs.title: Delegated native retrieval
docs.text:
The supplied UI and hosted strategy integrate the user authorization path. The UI obtains a delegated Search token through OBO and forwards it with x-client-search-token; the hosted connector passes the raw token in x-ms-query-source-authorization. The connector's workload credential authenticates transport to Search, not the user's entitlement to documents. This path needs no customer-written Toolbox integration.

Native permission filtering is enabled for the application index's user, group and RBAC scope fields. Indexing must populate the appropriate metadata; turning on filtering cannot reconstruct missing ACLs. Conversation uploads also require their conversation/uploader restrictions.

Source contracts differ. Work IQ uses a distinct app-audience assertion and x-ms-query-work-iq-source-authorization, not the Search token. Indexed SharePoint requires compatible permission-ingestion configuration; Fabric sources require compatible preview APIs and user permissions. A source registration or runtime connector alone does not establish that the complete deployment combination is supported.

Tokens do not belong in prompts, chat history, recovery checkpoints or user-supplied tool arguments. Required retrieval fails closed if credentials or source authorization are unavailable. Application authentication describes consent and allowed/denied-user acceptance.

docs.title: Ownership and connectivity
docs.text:
Platform Search setup reconciles named sources and knowledge bases from config/search/search.j2. Later provisioning can replace manual additions to those objects. Operator-owned sources and knowledge bases need distinct names; changes to platform-owned objects belong in reviewed templates. Knowledge-base updates must preserve all intended source references.

Source administration, ingestion and retrieval use separate permissions: the administrator manages knowledge objects; Search's ingestion identity reads the source and calls extraction/embedding services; the retrieval identity authenticates to Search; the end user's delegated identity authorizes protected content. A service role is not a substitute for user authorization.

Private deployments need both runtime-to-Search access and Search-to-source/model connectivity. The platform attempts to set generated Blob indexers to private execution, but skips that update if an indexer does not yet exist. Generated indexer state and shared private-link approvals still need validation before sensitive ingestion. See Network isolation.

docs.title: Acceptance and recovery
docs.text:
Acceptance includes successful source indexing where applicable, a known-answer query with the expected document reference, and separate allowed/denied-user tests. A denied result must exclude the restricted document and its citation. A missing-token failure calls for checking the compatible UI/runtime configuration, downstream consent and supported header path, not anonymous retrieval or broader managed-identity grants.

Configuration is cached in the running application. Approved changes require the Deploy full stack runbook to start a new hosted version. Recovery restores the previous compatible image and settings while retaining source documents and knowledge objects.

docs.title: Hosted agents
docs.text: Agent App Orchestrator runs as a container in Foundry Agent Service. The fresh default is DEPLOYMENT_TOPOLOGY=hosted-no-panel with maf_lite orchestration. The UI remains in Azure Container Apps. This page explains the hosting contract; the Deploy full stack runbook contains the ordered deployment and recovery procedures.

docs.title: Topologies
docs.text:
Hosted topology Orchestrator Administrative panel Agent Application Cosmos DB hosted-no-panel (default) Foundry hosted container Not deployed Not deployed

The table describes default application resources, not Foundry Agent Service's own backing resources. This layout does not activate history, feedback or operator access. Those capabilities have independent integration and validation gates. Agent App Ingestion is selected separately, as described in Ingestion and conversation uploads.

docs.title: Image and deployment handoff
docs.text: Hosted deployment separates foundation provisioning from application deployment. azd provision creates the project, registry, network and access prerequisites, not a running agent or a placeholder. azd deploy automatically builds the manifest-pinned orchestrator with the supported hosted startup command when needed, records an immutable digest, binds the image to the provisioned foundation and creates the agent version. No separate preparation command or second provision is needed; azd up performs the full workflow. Private builds still use the VNet's ACR Tasks agent pool.

docs.title: Redeploy the same image or prepare a new one
docs.text:
Change Deployment contract Same generated digest, matching source and startup provenance Deployment reuses the image. Missing image or changed generated source/startup provenance Deployment builds the manifest-pinned image and updates the handoff without reprovisioning. Changed hosted process environment or cached runtime settings A new agent version is required, potentially with the same compatible digest. Explicit digest without generated-source provenance Compatibility and registry availability are operator-owned. Deployment does not replace it automatically.

Generated images are reused only when the recorded source revision and startup command match. To supply an independently built image, set HOSTED_AGENT_IMAGE_VERSION to its canonical digest and clear HOSTED_AGENT_IMAGE_SOURCE_COMMIT and HOSTED_AGENT_IMAGE_STARTUP_COMMAND_SHA256. The image must be available in the selected registry and repository and already use the hosted entrypoint. Independent builds of the same source need not produce the same digest. The standalone preparation scripts remain optional compatibility commands; they are not required deployment steps.

The procedure is in application redeployment.

docs.title: Validation rules
docs.text:
Deployment settings distinguishes deployment inputs from App Configuration keys and hosted process environment.

HOSTED_AGENT_IMAGE_VERSION Immutable sha256: digest with 64 hexadecimal characters; tags are rejected. HOSTED_AGENT_RESOURCE_SCOPE Explicit delegated-user audience ending in /.default; not the UI API scope. HOSTED_AGENT_STARTUP_COMMAND Fixed to uvicorn src.api.hosted_entrypoint:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8088. HOSTED_AGENT_SSE_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS Stream idle timeout, default 60.

The supplied hosted-agent/azure.yaml declares the agent name, CPU, memory, protocols and startup command as literal fields. Its image and environment fields use azd interpolation. A custom application's source.imageDigest instead becomes AGENTLZ_IMAGE_DIGEST; it is not interchangeable with HOSTED_AGENT_IMAGE_VERSION. See source pinning.

docs.title: Runtime identities and access
docs.text:
Identity Responsibility Deployment principal Provisions resources, creates agent versions and reconciles authorized scoped grants. Foundry project managed identity Pulls the image through the registry grant. Actual deployed agent runtime principal Reads configuration and calls authorized dependencies. Delegated user Needs Foundry project/agent access and permission to requested data.

The post-deploy hook discovers the runtime principal and grants App Configuration Data Reader on the store and Cognitive Services OpenAI User on the Foundry account. If AUDIT_HMAC_KEY is a Key Vault reference, the bootstrap plan also includes Key Vault Secrets User on that individual secret. Native retrieval also uses Search Index Data Reader scoped to the configured Search resource for transport; native user/source authorization remains separate.

End-user source permissions, other secrets and caller permissions are outside this closed bootstrap set. Role reconciliation needs scoped role-assignment authority or an authorized administrator applying the reviewed plan. Hosted access recovery contains the operational checks.

Custom services reconcile declared capability profiles against the discovered runtime principal.

docs.title: Delegated UI invocation
docs.text:
Hosted composition routes the UI with CHAT_BACKEND=hosted_agent. The UI defaults to HOSTED_AGENT_AUTH_MODE=user_delegated. It exchanges the signed-in user's UI API token for the Foundry audience through OAuth on-behalf-of (OBO), without fallback to the UI managed identity. Agent Application access explains sign-in and consent. Successful invocation is not evidence of document-level authorization.

Foundry does not forward the invocation Authorization header unchanged. For native protected retrieval, the UI separately acquires a delegated Search token and forwards it in x-client-search-token. Both hosted adapters keep it request-local and the connector passes it to native Search permission enforcement. Missing required credentials fail before retrieval; they never trigger a service-identity retry.

Downstream Search authentication challenges terminate the current turn with a safe typed failure. The UI can request explicit interactive verification using the bounded claims; it does not replay the failed or partially streamed turn. A source denial without usable claims remains denied. See authentication recovery.

Native citation downloads stay on the authenticated UI and recheck source authorization at redemption. Shared Blob/ADLS reads use Storage OBO; conversation uploads require a fresh native Search ownership check before workload Blob transport. The bundled UI's retrieval-reader profile supplies the Search transport role, not the user's entitlement. See protected citation downloads for consent and source-access requirements.

The container's code still controls model calls, retrieval and tools. Portal instructions or tool attachments do not automatically reconfigure maf_lite; Agent tools describes the separate Toolbox extension boundary.

docs.title: Protocol and caller access
docs.text:
• Responses 2.0.0 is stateless. Non-null previous_response_id returns HTTP 422. Top-level conversation does not load managed history. Input contains bounded, ordered prior messages ending in the current user message.
  • Agent App UI uses /invocations?api-version=v1. Its conversation_id labels conversation-scoped retrieval; it is not permission to load history. The UI accepts response.conversation.id and response.conversation_id, and rejects malformed or conflicting IDs.
  • A delegated caller needs the endpoint interaction permission at the intended project or agent scope. Foundry Agent Consumer supplies least-privilege endpoint access; authoring roles are separate. Complete the login and caller-access setup. Deployment permission alone is insufficient.

Publish to Teams and M365 uses Bot Service authorization and the Activity endpoint. Connect Copilot Studio uses an authenticated Power Automate flow and VNet delegation, not the native connected-agent tool. These have different caller-identity contracts from the UI.

docs.title: Continuity, history and the administrative panel
docs.text:
Without continuity, multi-turn context lasts only for the active UI session. Reload, browser restart or a new chat loses that context. The hosted container does not read or write managed Conversations.

HOSTED_CONTINUITY_ENABLED defaults to false. Delegated continuity requires validated owner isolation, Responses protocol at least 2.0.0, and the middle-tier identity's reviewed agent-scoped UserIdentityImpersonation data action. HOSTED_CONVERSATION_OWNER_BINDING_VALIDATED is an evidence gate, not a way to grant those permissions. Provisioning leaves it false. When validated continuity is active, the UI sends the authorized transcript to the stateless container, which still does not load managed history.

Panel user routes additionally require actual panel deployment, PANEL_HISTORY_ENABLED and active continuity; otherwise they return HTTP 503. The panel's delegated enumeration and operator surfaces have separate gates, PANEL_HISTORY_OWNER_BINDING_VALIDATED and PANEL_OPERATOR_SURFACES_ENABLED. They remain false until their own authorization checks have evidence. Cosmos holds owner-index/feedback metadata; managed transcripts reside in Foundry. User feedback explains the missing UI integration.

docs.title: Configuration TLS compatibility
docs.text:
APP_CONFIG_TLS_COMPATIBILITY is an opt-in process environment variable, default false, read before remote configuration. It applies only to the orchestrator loader's configured App Configuration and Key Vault endpoints. The profile uses P-256 and TCP MSS 1200 while retaining certificate/hostname verification, custom CAs, TLS 1.2 or later, credentials and retries. It requires the actual HTTPS KEY_VAULT_URI; invalid input fails startup.

An App Configuration key cannot replace this bootstrap input. A changed value requires a new hosted version. The TLS diagnosis reference covers transport diagnosis without disabling certificate validation.

docs.title: Telemetry
docs.text: Prompt/completion capture is off by default. The deployment input HOSTED_AGENT_CAPTURE_MESSAGE_CONTENT maps to the hosted process variable OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_GENAI_CAPTURE_MESSAGE_CONTENT. A changed value requires a new agent version. Capture into Application Insights is a data-retention and privacy decision, not a prerequisite for chat.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
Agent Landing Zone connects deployment inputs, Azure infrastructure and application code through the Azure Developer CLI (azd). This page introduces those concepts for the Bicep and integrated Terraform implementations, so you can understand what the deployment does without memorizing commands or parameters.

A command-line interface (CLI) runs commands in a terminal. Bicep or Terraform describes Azure resources as code; azd coordinates their creation and application deployment. Azure Blob Storage stores files, and Azure AI Search indexes content so the application can retrieve relevant passages. An application programming interface (API) lets code send requests to a service.

An orchestrator coordinates model calls, retrieval and tools. The default Agent Application runs it in Foundry Agent Service with maf_lite, the supplied orchestration strategy (the code path that coordinates a turn). It has no administration panel and uses native Foundry IQ Blob ingestion, where Azure AI Search prepares Blob documents for retrieval.

The sections below explain how that application and its infrastructure are prepared. The Deploy infra only and Deploy full stack runbooks provide the execution steps.

docs.title: How to read deployment settings
docs.text:
A deployment parameter tells the template what to create or reuse, such as a private network or an existing hub. An azd environment groups the settings and deployment state for one deployment, such as development or production. Both infrastructure providers use the same operator inputs:

Input form Source Uppercase input, such as NETWORK_ISOLATION The selected azd environment. The hooks resolve documented mappings before provisioning. Structured value, such as modelDeploymentList The root main.parameters.json, inside parameters.<name>.value. Keep arrays, objects, booleans and numbers in their native JSON types.

For example, NETWORK_ISOLATION=true selects private networking. Deployment inputs and the root parameter file are resolved before provisioning. For Terraform, a typed adapter generates the ignored infra/terraform/main.tfvars.json. The generated infra/main.parameters.json supports shared preflight diagnostics; Bicep uses that file for its deployment. The Deployment settings reference lists inputs and defaults; choose the provider-specific Deploy infra only or Deploy full stack runbook for their application order.

Application-specific runtime settings

Runtime settings control an application's behavior and vary by application. Here they describe Agent Application, the supplied reference app. Its settings are usually stored in Azure App Configuration.

docs.title: Repository boundaries
docs.text:
The platform repository coordinates infrastructure and application deployment. The Agent Application's runtime code lives in separate component repositories.

Area Responsibility Bicep infrastructure: platform infra/ Bicep source for Azure resources, identities and access. Terraform infrastructure: platform infra/terraform/ AVM composition, complementary resources, generated typed inputs, native outputs and committed provider lock file. Platform integration: root files, scripts/ and config/ Selects the application, composes deployment parameters, configures provisioned services and coordinates deployment. Runtime component repositories Own Agent App UI, Agent App Orchestrator (strategies and tools), and optional Agent App Ingestion. The manifest identifies their repositories and source pins.

Deployment uses the product's infrastructure source for the selected provider.

docs.title: The manifest records a validated combination
docs.text:
manifest.json records the platform release and each Agent Application component's repository, release tag and exact Git commit. A Git commit identifies an exact source revision; a tag is a readable label for a version. These identify the code versions validated together.

The hooks fetch selected Container App components into sibling directories and verify their commits. Hosted image preparation fetches the pinned orchestrator separately. Deploying the reference app needs no repository forks.

The Agent Application's app-definition.json also records component commits and is validated against the manifest. A modified combination needs its own integration validation. See Custom applications for repository customization and pinning rules.

docs.title: Parameters describe the environment
docs.text:
The checked-in root main.parameters.json maps deployment inputs to infrastructure parameters. Values can be literals or references to the selected azd environment's variables. Inline defaults apply where declared; other unset inputs can use Bicep defaults.

Before provisioning, the hooks validate the provider/application binding, resolve the shared hosting topology and apply environment inputs.

Provider Generated deployment input Bicep infra/main.parameters.json Terraform infra/terraform/main.tfvars.json

Terraform renders backend settings from infra/terraform/provider.conf.json. Its generated infra/main.parameters.json is only a shared preflight artifact, not the Terraform deployment input.

Terraform cloud and backend records

The adapter qualifies public, usgovernment or china and generates the matching azureCloud context and backend environment. See Azure cloud settings.

An immutable private backend record is created on first use before settings are persisted and verified thereafter. Clean runners need the original backend, group and application/environment bindings, not reconstructed files.

Edit the source, not the generated output

Use documented environment inputs and root main.parameters.json. Do not edit generated infra/main.parameters.json, infra/terraform/main.tfvars.json or .azure/ inputs. See Deployment settings for inputs and defaults.

An application definition describes the selected application's components and capabilities. The environment records that definition's id on first provision and rejects a different one later. This identifies the deployed application; it is not a Microsoft Entra ID application registration ID.

Microsoft Entra ID handles sign-in and service identities in an organization's directory, called a tenant. An application registration describes a sign-in application to that service. Custom application selection therefore happens before the first provision.

Hosting, orchestration strategy and ingestion selection are separate decisions. For example, choosing a hosted orchestrator does not select an ingestion path. The configuration and application definition must form a supported combination. The hosted runtime rejects unsupported strategies rather than silently switching strategy or host. The multimodal and nl2sql strategies are not supported by this host.

docs.title: Deployment lifecycle
docs.text:
The root azure.yaml selects the infrastructure provider/path and registers PowerShell and shell lifecycle hooks. Bicep at infra/ remains the default. To use Terraform, configure infra.provider: terraform, infra.path: infra/terraform and infra.module: main once before a new environment's first provision. This selection applies to the checkout, not independently to each environment in it. Use the selected provider for provisioning, updates and removal.

The shared hooks configure Azure services and coordinate application deployment.

Stage What the platform does Before azd up (preup) Validates the application definition and checks that it matches the environment's recorded application. Before provisioning (preprovision) Validates provider/application binding, resolves shared topology, generates provider-specific typed inputs and runs preflight checks. After provisioning (postprovision) Configures Azure services, reconciles application access and publishes runtime settings and outputs. Before deployment (predeploy) Checks infrastructure readiness and the recorded application, validates topology and required connectivity, then coordinates the selected application deployments.

azd provision includes service configuration through its post-provision hook. Some Container Apps initially contain placeholder images; azd deploy replaces them with the selected application code. azd up runs both stages. Provisioning does not build or publish application images; reapplying infrastructure must preserve application-managed images and revisions. All flat Terraform outputs feed azd and those shared hooks automatically; operators do not copy outputs into application projects.

The Terraform backend uses existing Azure Storage outside workload teardown. Native azd disables state locking. Shared and production state uses one authorized executor with queued, non-canceling operations per backend state identity; see the single-writer policy.

Container App deployment builds verified component code through each component's azure.yaml. Hosted orchestration uses the prepared image described below. Custom applications supply their own definitions and projects for deployment.

docs.title: App Configuration carries runtime settings
docs.text: Deployment inputs describe what to create. Runtime settings describe how applications use the resulting services.

docs.title: Who publishes settings
docs.text:
Provisioning and configuration publish settings to Azure App Configuration under the agent-lz label.

Terraform owns foundation connections and model metadata. Shared defaults seed only missing keys, while the runtime publisher updates its owned settings from the declared parameter document and selected environment.

Labels, content types and Key Vault-reference metadata follow the configuration ownership contract.

docs.title: How applications load settings
docs.text: The Agent Application loaders also select other labels, which can affect which setting takes precedence. Bootstrap values such as the store endpoint must be available before remote configuration can load.

docs.title: Secrets and environment boundaries
docs.text:
Secrets belong in Key Vault and are referenced rather than copied into checked-in settings.

The same label is used across environments, so separation depends on distinct configuration, identities and data, as described in Environment boundaries.

Local .azure/ state is private deployment state, not a source-controlled input file. Child workspaces receive copies and need the same protection. Terraform's backend and group records are also required for state-scoped teardown; output refresh does not replace them.

See Deployment settings for setting names, sources and reload requirements.

docs.title: Why hosted agents need image preparation
docs.text:
A Foundry hosted agent needs an immutable image before its agent version can be deployed. That creates a bootstrap dependency on the registry and Foundry resources.

An image digest identifies the built container image by its content. It is not a source commit or a mutable image tag.

  1. Infrastructure prerequisites. Initial provisioning creates and configures the required Azure services and access rules.
  2. Automatic image preparation during deploy. The deployment hook builds the pinned orchestrator and its hosted entrypoint image when needed, recording the digest and build details.
  3. Application handoff during deploy. The hook binds the image to the provisioned project, registry and network metadata without another provision.
  4. Application publication. Deployment creates the hosted agent version and deploys the other selected application components.

Image preparation does not start the agent, and provisioning does not create the running data-plane agent version. Deploy-only reuses a compatible generated image, or rebuilds when generated source/startup provenance changes. Operators use azd provision followed by azd deploy, or azd up; there is no required standalone preparation command.

The same source pins do not guarantee the same image digest when images are built independently. If a promotion process requires the identical image, its digest and registry availability need separate preservation and verification.

The full-stack runbooks for Bicep and Terraform provide execution steps. For strategy eligibility and image behavior, see Agent hosting.

docs.title: From understanding to deployment
docs.text:
The planning references explain deployment design, the Sizing & cost planner. For execution, choose the outcome and then the provider:

  • Deploy infra only: With Bicep or With Terraform.
  • Deploy full stack: With Bicep or With Terraform.

Those runbooks contain the prerequisites, topology-specific sequence and validation steps.

docs.title: Ingestion and conversation uploads
docs.text:
Foundry IQ provides the standard source-ingestion path. Conversation attachments and custom processing are separate capabilities that can require optional Agent App Ingestion.

This page explains those boundaries. Deployment steps are in the Deploy full stack runbook; source and index inputs are described in Deployment settings.

docs.title: 1. Standard ingestion with Foundry IQ
docs.text:
The default source is Azure Blob Storage, with FOUNDRY_IQ_PATTERN=azureBlob and container documents. Azure AI Search, which powers Foundry IQ, creates and manages the indexing pipeline for this knowledge source. It extracts content, splits it into smaller passages (chunks), generates embeddings (vectors used for similarity search) and populates an index used by the knowledge base.

Agent App Ingestion is not required for this path. New Agent Application environments default to DEPLOY_INGESTION_CONTAINER_APP=false.

Source documents belong in the configured Blob container and optional folder, not in a chat attachment. Search's ingestion identity needs access to storage and the configured extraction and embedding services. The default permission metadata is ["rbacScope"]; ingestion permissions and the querying user's authorization remain separate requirements. Microsoft's Blob knowledge-source guide describes the managed pipeline and service requirements.

Successful ingestion alone does not establish protected retrieval. The built-in UI/hosted native path forwards a separately delegated Search token; ingestion must still record correct permissions and acceptance must prove allow/deny behavior. Application access describes the OBO contract.

Foundry also supports native SharePoint options, including previews:

Native option What happens to the content Foundry IQ indexedSharePoint source A service-managed pipeline copies and processes SharePoint content into a Search index. No Agent App Ingestion is required by the service. Foundry IQ remoteSharePoint source The knowledge base queries Microsoft 365 at retrieval time. It does not copy the SharePoint corpus into a landing-zone index. Retrieved text still reaches the agent and model. Foundry Agent Service SharePoint tool The agent calls a native tool backed by Microsoft 365 retrieval, outside the knowledge-base source list. It does not require the custom ingestion application.

These product options are not all wired into Agent Application. The native indexed SharePoint path includes source registration, permission ingestion and delegated Search authorization. Remote retrieval and native tools need their own connection, consent and trusted delegated-user integration. Native tool calls require the user's identity, not application-only access. SharePoint explains the supported bindings and administrator prerequisites. Preview status is a governance consideration, not a reason to assume custom ingestion is required.

The accelerator's ingestion-free validation accepts native Blob or an explicitly bound, independently populated Search index as its primary selection. Native indexed SharePoint is an additional configured knowledge source; enabling it does not require Agent App Ingestion or replace the primary pattern setting. Other Microsoft product options are not automatically supported deployment selections in the accelerator.

docs.title: 2. Conversation file uploads
docs.text:
A chat attachment is processed for one conversation, not added to the shared native Blob corpus. This path requires Agent App Ingestion, its reachable endpoint and a compatible Search index. Alongside the default native Blob source, the additional conversation searchIndex source needs FOUNDRY_IQ_CONVERSATION_UPLOAD_ENABLED=true. The flag is invalid without the ingestion app.

With DEPLOY_INGESTION_CONTAINER_APP=false, Agent App UI hides attachment controls and rejects server uploads and client preflight before resolving an ingestion endpoint or Dapr fallback. Setting it to true permits the upload path. Retrieval uses the built-in delegated Search route and native index permissions; enabling processing does not grant access to uploaded content.

The UI's attachment controls require authenticated access. Anonymous Copilot sessions cannot upload. The chat handler accepts PDFs, up to five files, 15 MiB per file and 25 MiB total. Hosted uploads require the UI's existing hosted conversation identifier. A text turn establishes it in the non-continuity hosted path; continuity-enabled chat does not populate that upload identifier.

The UI requires a valid object ID from its authenticated uploader context before calling ingestion. Ingestion stamps every chunk with that uploader in metadata_security_user_ids, an empty metadata_security_group_ids array, an empty metadata_security_rbac_scope and the conversation ID. The platform enables native permission filtering over these fields.

Conversation scope uses the hosted backend's conversation namespace, not the local UI thread ID. The same identifier must reach the indexed upload and retrieval filter. Native Search authorizes the uploader from the delegated Search token and the ingested user ACL; the additional filter restricts results to the current conversationId. Neither a conversation ID nor an opaque hosted user/partition identifier grants document access.

Missing required delegation or conversation scope stops retrieval. A configured upload source cannot be silently skipped to return only shared-corpus results, and a failed source cannot be retried without the user's credential. The conversation PDF reference describes source bindings. Application access describes the integrated identity path and consent requirements.

docs.title: 3. Custom ingestion only when needed
docs.text:
Agent App Ingestion is useful when the managed source does not meet processing requirements, or when conversation uploads or the application's custom SharePoint jobs are required. Its format-specific processing performs chunking and embedding generation and writes content to Search. An independent pipeline can instead populate a compatible index exposed through a Foundry IQ searchIndex source.

The optional application's SharePoint connector uses Microsoft Graph application credentials and indexing/purge jobs. It copies content and permission metadata into Search; permission synchronization and query-time enforcement still need validation.

Every selected item's supported ACLs are reconciled on each SharePoint index run, even when content is unchanged, without re-downloading or embedding that content. Grants and revocations replace stored permissions on all affected documents and chunks. See SharePoint permission synchronization for scheduling, filter boundaries, inherited-permission support and recovery.

It is separate from native SharePoint knowledge sources and the native Foundry tool. Its SHAREPOINT_* credentials are not the SHAREPOINT_REMOTE_* retrieval settings. Secrets belong in Key Vault.

For the bundled Agent Application, DEPLOY_INGESTION_CONTAINER_APP selects the optional component through the Deploy full stack runbook, not a runtime-only edit. Existing environments retain their recorded selection; custom application definitions retain their declared components. Selection does not change retrieval bindings or document authorization. Omitting the application does not delete deployed resources, indexed documents or identity grants; retirement needs separate authorization.

Native upload downloads repeat authorization through Search for the exact document, conversation and authenticated uploader before workload Blob access. A signed citation selector or known conversation ID is insufficient. Shared-source Blob/ADLS downloads instead use user-delegated Storage access. See protected citation downloads.

For every path, acceptance includes a document that an allowed user can retrieve with its citation and that a denied user cannot retrieve. Source permissions, query-time enforcement and private-network connectivity require separate validation. Private Blob ingestion is covered in Network isolation.

docs.title: Images and voice
docs.text: Agent Application can ground text answers in image descriptions extracted from documents. This differs from passing an image or audio directly to a model. The default hosted maf_lite path uses text input and retrieved text. This page explains capability boundaries; the Deploy full stack runbook contains deployment procedures.

docs.title: Supported content
docs.text: Content Hosted application behavior Diagrams in a shared collection Native Foundry IQ Blob ingestion can produce image descriptions when its model and extraction requirements are met. Conversation PDF Optional Agent App Ingestion processes uploads; native Search permissions and a conversation filter authorize hosted retrieval. Screenshot or standalone image Not accepted by the supplied hosted input adapter or PDF upload handler. Voice No supplied capture, transcription, realtime audio or playback integration.

docs.title: Document image grounding
docs.text:
Native Blob ingestion can verbalize images during document processing. The knowledge base then returns extracted content to the orchestrator; the model receives text, not the original image.

This path uses RETRIEVAL_BACKEND=foundry_iq, FOUNDRY_IQ_PATTERN=azureBlob, FOUNDRY_IQ_KNOWLEDGE_SOURCE_KIND=azureBlob and FOUNDRY_IQ_CONTENT_EXTRACTION_MODE=standard. Agent App Ingestion is not required.

The provisioning template sets disableImageVerbalization=false, but only supplies chatCompletionModel for its supported Content Understanding model names. gpt-4.1 is supported; the default gpt-5-nano is not in that allowlist. The flag alone therefore does not establish working image verbalization in a fresh deployment. Standard extraction also requires a compatible region, Foundry AI Services endpoint and embedding deployment. Blob source prerequisites describe service requirements.

In main.parameters.json, the chat entry of modelDeploymentList uses canonical_name: CHAT_DEPLOYMENT_NAME; model.name identifies the family and name identifies the deployment. A model change affects availability, quota and extraction compatibility. Deployment settings identifies the configuration inputs. The rendered source's model binding and extracted diagram content are the evidence of successful processing, not the model name alone.

The ingestion identity's source/model access is independent of the user's retrieval permissions. Private connectivity follows Network isolation. Protected hosted retrieval uses the integrated delegated identity path and still needs allow/deny validation; image extraction does not authorize users.

docs.title: Conversation PDFs
docs.text:
DEPLOY_INGESTION_CONTAINER_APP defaults to false, so fresh deployments hide and reject uploads. Optional Agent App Ingestion is required for eligible PDF attachments, as described in Ingestion and conversation uploads.

With a native Blob primary source, conversation retrieval requires FOUNDRY_IQ_CONVERSATION_UPLOAD_ENABLED=true and provisioned FOUNDRY_IQ_CONVERSATION_KNOWLEDGE_SOURCE_NAME. The name identifies a Search knowledge source, not a URL or conversation ID. Keep the source and retrieval API settings compatible with the configured knowledge base. A missing or failed configured upload source stops required retrieval rather than silently returning only shared-corpus results.

The UI needs an established hosted conversation ID and an eligible signed-in session. It accepts at most five PDFs, 15 MiB each and 25 MiB combined. Anonymous embedded sessions cannot upload.

The UI validates the authenticated uploader's object ID before ingestion. Every uploaded chunk receives that user's ACL and the hosted conversation ID; group and RBAC grants remain empty. Native Search evaluates that ACL using the delegated Search token, while an additional conversation filter prevents results from other conversations. The runtime does not treat an opaque hosted partition key as an uploader identity or decode the forwarded token to invent one. Processing confirmation alone is not retrieval-isolation evidence: test both the uploader and a different user, including citations and download attempts.

Agent App Ingestion's separate MULTIMODAL setting controls figure extraction and captioning in its custom pipeline. It does not enable direct screenshot input. Scanned or diagram-only PDFs depend on the extracted content.

docs.title: Evidence and configuration lifecycle
docs.text:
Grounded image answers depend on completed ingestion, extracted content, a compatible model binding and the intended source reference. A processed PDF can still be absent from retrieval; shared-source answers alone do not prove conversation-upload retrieval works.

Runtime configuration is cached. A changed hosted setting needs a new agent version; affected UI and ingestion processes also need to reload. Source/model changes follow the Deploy full stack runbook. The pinned API remains part of the application contract rather than an independent setting to change without compatibility validation.

docs.title: Direct image and voice extensions
docs.text:
Screenshot input requires caller and adapter development to validate and forward image content to a compatible model. Microsoft's vision input guide describes model APIs, not an enabled Agent Application feature.

Voice requires client/service integration for capture, transcription or realtime audio, and playback. The Realtime audio guide describes those APIs. Bring your own app covers the application boundary. Both extensions need authentication, input limits and source authorization when connected to retrieval.

docs.title: Network isolation
docs.text:
Use private networking for production and workloads with sensitive data. Set NETWORK_ISOLATION=true explicitly before provisioning. The template's current default is false; that default is not the recommended production configuration.

Reserve public service endpoints for organization-approved, short-lived evaluations or demonstrations with synthetic or non-sensitive data. Public endpoints still require authentication and authorization, but those checks do not make them private. Do not disable isolation to work around connectivity or deployment failures.

This page explains connectivity, DNS and build requirements rather than deployment steps. How it works introduces the input formats and deployment lifecycle.

Both providers use the root main.parameters.json examples on this page. For Terraform, preprovision generates typed inputs automatically; see the Terraform input procedure.

A private endpoint gives a service a private IP address in a VNet. Private DNS directs its normal hostname to that address. A virtual private network (VPN) connects an authorized remote computer or network to the VNet.

A jumpbox is a virtual machine (VM) used for administration; Azure Bastion provides remote access to it. A NAT gateway provides outbound address translation. None of these connections grants permission to read service data.

With NETWORK_ISOLATION=true, Agent Landing Zone uses private endpoints and private DNS for the deployed workload services. With the default empty allowedIpRanges, public access to those service endpoints is disabled. Azure Resource Manager remains public; telemetry and optional public ingress have separate settings.

An explicit, nonempty allowedIpRanges in main.parameters.json enables IP-restricted public access on services that support those rules, even with isolation enabled. Those public paths and any reused network or DNS resources remain part of the connectivity design.

The Deploy infra only and Deploy full stack runbooks contain the procedures. The Azure DevOps runbook covers optional pipeline automation. Deployment choices explains standalone and hub integration. An AI Gateway governs model requests, not workload networking or user access. Private endpoints, DNS, routes, firewall rules and authorization remain necessary.

With the resource group destinations, locally owned private endpoints default to the resolved network group, which can differ from their services' groups. The explicit AZURE_PE_RESOURCE_GROUP_NAME override and existing-VNet/SIDE_BY_SIDE precedence in Deployment settings still apply.

Teams and Microsoft 365 Copilot publication

Publish to Teams and M365 adds a manual, source-IP-filtered public exception for the Foundry Activity route while Foundry and Bot Service public network access stays disabled. Microsoft calls this a source IP-filtered Activity Protocol public endpoint.

Channel messages use public HTTPS, not Private Link, so this path is not private end to end. If public agent ingress is prohibited, do not use that publication path. Other Foundry APIs remain private, and the template does not enable this exception.

The Connect Copilot Studio runbook describes an authenticated agent flow and Power Platform VNet delegation to reach the Foundry private endpoint; it does not require the Activity-route public exception.

docs.title: What changes with isolation
docs.text:
Area NETWORK_ISOLATION=false NETWORK_ISOLATION=true Workload service access Public endpoints, with service authentication and authorization Private endpoints by default DNS Public DNS Private DNS zones linked to the VNet Jumpbox, Azure Bastion, NAT gateway Not deployed by default Deployed by default Container image builds Local Docker or regular ACR Tasks ACR Task agent pool inside the VNet by default Post-provision and deploy Run from an authorized host that can reach the endpoints Run from an authorized host connected to the VNet

Note

The ACR Task agent pool is created only for isolated deployments. When isolation is off, supported components can build with local Docker or regular ACR Tasks. No pool is created, even if DEPLOY_ACR_TASK_AGENT_POOL is true.

docs.title: Isolation and provisioning
docs.text: NETWORK_ISOLATION=true is resolved before provisioning. The selected topology, subnet creation flags and resource ownership determine which subnets are created. Choose who manages them before first provision.

docs.title: Choose subnet ownership
docs.text:
These choices apply with network isolation enabled. Hub connectivity and DNS remain separate decisions.

Network choice USE_EXISTING_VNET DEPLOY_SUBNETS Responsibility New VNet and subnets false true The template creates the VNet and selected subnets. Existing VNet, template-managed subnets true true Supply EXISTING_VNET_RESOURCE_ID; the template creates/updates selected subnets. Existing VNet, externally managed subnets true false Supply the VNet ID; its owner prepares every subnet required by enabled consumers.

Using an existing VNet does not make deployment read-only. Individual creation flags can exclude subnets from template management. See the network selection examples.

docs.title: Default subnets
docs.text:
The new VNet's default address space is 192.168.0.0/21. Names and ranges can be overridden using the subnet inputs.

Purpose Default name Default CIDR Foundry Agent Service agent-subnet 192.168.0.0/24 Container Apps environment aca-environment-subnet 192.168.1.0/24 Foundry/grounding private endpoints pe-subnet 192.168.2.0/26 Bastion AzureBastionSubnet 192.168.2.64/26 Firewall AzureFirewallSubnet 192.168.2.128/26 VPN/ExpressRoute reservation GatewaySubnet 192.168.2.192/26 Application Gateway AppGatewaySubnet 192.168.3.0/27 Jumpbox jumpbox-subnet 192.168.3.64/27 Build agents devops-build-agents-subnet 192.168.3.96/27 Application private endpoints application-pe-subnet 192.168.3.128/26 Basic firewall management AzureFirewallManagementSubnet 192.168.3.192/26 Power Platform powerplatform-subnet 192.168.4.0/24 AI Gateway ai-gateway-subnet 192.168.5.0/24

docs.title: Subnet delegations
docs.text:
• Foundry Agent Service and Container Apps environment: Microsoft.App/environments.
  • Power Platform: Microsoft.PowerPlatform/enterprisePolicies.
  • AI Gateway: Microsoft.Web/serverFarms.
  • All other subnets in this plan: no delegation.

Firewall data subnet creation defaults to the local firewall requirement. The management subnet is used only by a standalone Basic firewall. GatewaySubnet is opt-in. The table is an address plan, not an unconditional resource inventory; shared-hub services do not require these reservations in the spoke.

Creation is not service selection. A false subnet creation flag does not disable its consumers: any enabled consumer still needs a valid subnet. With isolation off, no VNet or subnets are provisioned.

Prepared subnets are not deployed services. These reservations do not deploy APIM or VPN/ExpressRoute gateways, create a Power Platform enterprise policy, or associate a Power Platform environment. Those integrations need separate setup.

Enabled application Cosmos DB, Key Vault, App Configuration, Container Apps, ACR and Azure Monitor Private Link Scope endpoints use the application private endpoint subnet. Foundry/grounding endpoints use pe-subnet by default. Application endpoints never fall back to the Foundry subnet, including when application subnet creation is disabled. This separation is independent of resource group count.

Keep the reserved name GatewaySubnet; do not attach an NSG, default-route UDR or delegation to it. AI Gateway uses APIM Standard v2/Premium v2 outbound VNet integration, with a subnet of /27 or larger, delegated to Microsoft.Web/serverFarms and associated with an NSG. Preserve an outbound HTTPS path to Azure Key Vault. No reserved subnet name is required for APIM; do not place APIM private endpoints in its delegated integration subnet.

The Power Platform /24 is a capacity default, not a platform minimum. Size for environment demand: approximately 25–30 IPs per production environment or 6–10 per nonproduction environment, plus five subnet-reserved IPs. See Power Platform subnet sizing.

Azure Resource Manager (ARM) creates and manages Azure resources through a public control plane, but azd provision also runs lifecycle hooks. An existing environment can need private App Configuration access before ARM deployment to resolve its topology. Post-provision also needs private connectivity, so an unconnected host cannot complete every stage.

The matching deployment runbook therefore requires a connected host. The default Foundry hosted deployment automatically prepares its image and application handoff during azd deploy, as described in Deploy full stack.

docs.title: Private network access
docs.text:
Private services can be reached through:

  • Point-to-site or site-to-site VPN into the landing zone VNet or a peered hub.
  • A VM or build agent in the VNet or a peered VNet, with private DNS zone access.
  • The jumpbox VM deployed by the landing zone, reached through Azure Bastion.

docs.title: Jumpbox access
docs.text:
The default jumpbox is a Windows VM. Unless overridden, its administrator user is testvmuser. The password is supplied through the secure vmAdminPassword provisioning input, not a documented Key Vault secret. Unavailable credentials require an authorized administrator's approved reset procedure, without exposing passwords in shell history or logs.

Azure Bastion provides portal access to the VM. It still needs the deployment prerequisites. Docker is not installed by default and is unnecessary for ACR Task agent-pool builds.

docs.title: Connected-host requirements
docs.text:
