docs.title: One layer, two jobs
docs.text:
This is the reframe that matters most in the updated blueprint:

Agent Operations delivers the experience — and its first line of trust.

Job What it means ① Delivers the experience (Intelligence) The agents that deliver the AI experience: any agent type, grounded in your data (IQ), using your tools (MCP), collaborating agent-to-agent, on any model. ② Carries agent-level trust (Trust, built in) End-to-end traces, AI evals, red-teaming, and guardrails — tuned to each agent's type and objective. The builder owns this.

Trust is not the job of a couple of security controls off to the side. It starts inside Agent Operations, and three platform controls — Governance Hub, Agent Management, and Security Foundation — then make it hold at scale.

The layer that delivers intelligence is also the first line of trust.

docs.title: The two roles of Foundry: runtime and observability plane
docs.text:
This distinction is the single most important thing to understand about Layer 2 — and the most commonly missed.

Important

Foundry plays two independent roles. You can adopt either one, or both.

① Foundry as a runtime — you host agents in Foundry (prompt agents and hosted agents). These agents automatically inherit every Foundry capability: tracing, evaluations, guardrails, identity, IQ grounding, MCP tools, and control-plane operations, with little or no wiring.

② Foundry as the agent control plane for agents running elsewhere — agents on AKS, Azure Container Apps, other clouds, or on-premises forward OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic traces into Foundry-connected Application Insights. They then light up in the same observability plane — centralized traces, AI evaluations, quality and safety signals, and fleet operations — without being hosted in Foundry at all.

        ┌─────────────────────── ROLE 1: RUNTIME ───────────────────────┐
        │  Prompt agents  ·  Hosted agents (BYO container/framework)    │
        │  → inherit tracing, evals, guardrails, identity, IQ, MCP      │
        └───────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────┘
                                        │
                                        ▼
                        ┌───────────────────────────────┐
                        │   MICROSOFT FOUNDRY           │
                        │   Control Plane               │
                        │   • end-to-end traces         │
                        │   • AI evaluations            │
                        │   • guardrails & controls     │
                        │   • fleet-wide operations     │
                        └───────────────▲───────────────┘
                                        │
                        Foundry-connected Application Insights
                                        ▲
                                        │  OTel GenAI semantic traces
        ┌───────────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────────┐
        │  ROLE 2: OBSERVABILITY PLANE FOR AGENTS RUNNING ELSEWHERE     │
        │  AKS · Azure Container Apps · other clouds · on-premises      │
        │  Copilot Studio · third-party runtimes · any OTel emitter     │
        └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Why this matters commercially and architecturally:

  • It decouples the hosting decision from the governance decision. A customer who will not (or cannot) host agents in Foundry can still standardize observability, evaluation, and compliance signals on Foundry.
  • It removes the false choice between "adopt Foundry as a runtime" and "no Foundry at all." The observability plane is adoptable on its own.
  • It is the path through which Platform (BYO) and third-party agents reach Layer 2.
  • The managed runtime is a convenience; the observability is the strategic value.

Think of Foundry as the unified control plane for running and observing agents — whether you choose to host them there or not.

docs.title: Role 1 · Foundry as agent runtime
docs.text: Foundry provides a managed runtime for all agent form factors — and it is model-agnostic and framework-agnostic, so teams adopt new models and frameworks without sacrificing enterprise guarantees.

docs.title: Agent form factors
docs.text: Form factor What it is Prompt agents Declarative, low-code agents defined primarily by instructions, tools, and knowledge — the fastest path from idea to a working agent. Hosted agents Custom-code agents built with open agent frameworks, packaged as containers and deployed into Foundry. The unified runtime foundation for code-first work. Workflow agents Longer-running, orchestrated processes. Coding agents Development-time agents that use the same primitives — agent loops, tools, knowledge, memory, evals, observability.

docs.title: Hosted agents — deploy custom code built with open frameworks
docs.text:
Instead of managing containers, scaling policies, and runtime isolation yourself, Foundry provides a hosted execution environment purpose-built for agent workloads:

  • Framework-agnostic by design — keep your preferred open-source agent framework; Foundry Agent Service handles deployment, scaling, security, and operations
  • Long-running workflows, background tasks, and cross-agent collaboration handled within a managed runtime that scales automatically
  • Session-level isolation and fast startup for multi-tenant agent workloads
  • Observability and governance still built in — trace execution flows, monitor tool calls, and enforce policies without custom infrastructure

Build however you want, and run with enterprise-grade reliability and control.

docs.title: What hosted agents inherit automatically
docs.text:
This is the practical payoff of choosing Foundry as the runtime — these are enterprise defaults, not integration projects:

Inherited capability Detail Identity Distinct agent identities with full auditability; no stored secrets. Each project and each published agent gets its own Entra Agent ID. Token management & OBO Built-in token handling plus on-behalf-of flows for user-scoped actions Tracing Connect Application Insights and tracing turns on automatically — no code Evaluations Agent evaluators run without refactoring the agent Guardrails Runtime and control-plane content safety, applied at the right lifecycle point Context & tools Foundry IQ grounding and MCP tool access, assembled by the platform Governance AI Gateway controls and continuous monitoring for responsible AI Distribution Publish straight into Microsoft 365 and Teams; deploy from GitHub

docs.title: Composition: skills
docs.text: The primary unit of composition is shifting from multi-agent orchestration to skills — reusable, governable capabilities that can improve over time and be shared across agents, rather than logic locked inside a single agent's orchestration graph.

docs.title: Multi-agent patterns
docs.text: Agents can call each other as tools (Connected Agents), passing tasks between specialized agents to solve complex problems collaboratively — with A2A for cross-platform agent collaboration.

docs.title: Role 2 · Foundry as the universal observability plane
docs.text:
The observability story is not limited to agents running on Foundry's managed runtime. It extends to your entire agent ecosystem.

Most enterprises have agents everywhere: SaaS agents like Copilot, platform agents hosted on AKS or ACA, agents on other clouds or on-premises, and third-party agents from other vendors. The question is how to get a single pane of glass across all of them.

docs.title: The mechanism: OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions
docs.text:
Any agent — regardless of where it runs — can be configured to emit GenAI semantic logs using OTel. Those logs flow through Foundry-connected Application Insights into Foundry, and once they are in Foundry you unlock the full ecosystem: end-to-end agent traces, continuous AI evaluations, compliance controls, and quality and safety signals — all in one place.

   Your agent (anywhere)
   AKS · ACA · other cloud · on-prem · 3rd-party · Copilot Studio
            │
            │  1. Instrument with OTel GenAI semantic conventions
            │     (gen_ai.* spans — pro-code SDKs emit the richest detail)
            ▼
   2. Export to Foundry-connected Application Insights
            │
            ▼
   3. Microsoft Foundry
            ├── End-to-end agent traces
            ├── Continuous AI evaluations
            ├── Compliance controls
            ├── Quality & safety signals
            └── Fleet-wide operations

It doesn't matter if the agent is a Copilot extension, a custom agent on AKS, or a third-party solution — they all light up in the same observability plane.

docs.title: The semantic conventions that make this work
docs.text:
Microsoft is among the leading contributors to OpenTelemetry and the related W3C communities, and those contributions flow into services across the portfolio. Specific to generative-AI observability:

Convention set What it standardizes LLM semantics Model calls, prompts, completions, token usage, latency Evaluation semantics Evaluation results carried as first-class telemetry Events semantics Discrete agent lifecycle and decision events MCP conventions Tool invocation over Model Context Protocol Azure MCP Server instrumentation Out-of-the-box instrumentation for MCP servers

Because it is an open standard, a wide variety of agentic frameworks are supported — and because you own the instrumentation in your own code, you can capture the richest detail available.

docs.title: Across the full lifecycle
docs.text: Phase What observability gives you Development Trace agent behavior, run evaluations, and catch issues before anything hits production Production The same observability keeps running continuously — so you are never flying blind

docs.title: Open and interoperable by design
docs.text:
Foundry Observability is built to integrate with your existing monitoring estate, not replace it:

  • Azure Monitor — Application Insights and Log Analytics underneath; Azure Workbooks, dashboards, and Grafana on top
  • APM partners — designed to integrate with third-party APM tooling (for example Dynatrace, New Relic, Datadog) rather than compete with them
  • Export and integration are straightforward, so customers retain control of their own telemetry data

docs.title: Every agent gets context, tools, collaboration, and any model
docs.text:
Agents never run alone. Whatever you build, every agent gets:

Capability Delivered by 🧠 Context · IQ Agentic retrieval through Foundry IQ — grounded in your data, moving beyond classic RAG by blending retrieval, memory, and tool signals into coherent, task-aware context 🧰 Tools · MCP A rich selection of MCP tools — 1,400+ MCP-enabled connectors, plus REST and Logic Apps abstracted behind consistent, governed endpoints 🤝 Collaboration Agent-to-agent (A2A); Connected Agents let agents call each other as tools 🎛️ Any model Foundry Model Catalog, GPU-hosted, or externally hosted — with API compatibility for leading model platforms 🧩 Memory Managed memory, managed conversations, agentic/episodic memory, or a BYO memory store

And agent-level trust, built in: 🔍 Traces · 📊 Evals · 🎯 Red-teaming · 🚧 Guardrails

docs.title: Context engineering
docs.text:
Agent reliability degrades when tools are overloaded or unranked, knowledge is poorly structured, or prompts are naïvely constructed. Classic RAG makes this worse — long-context execution often dilutes or drops critical signals (the "lost in the middle" problem).

The platform's answer is to treat context as a first-class primitive assembled at runtime: selecting, ranking, and composing knowledge, memory, and tool outputs based on the agent's intent and state — rather than static prompt wiring done by the developer. Context becomes observable and improvable, not just an input.

The IQ family compounds this across the estate: Foundry IQ contributes curated institutional knowledge, Work IQ contributes flow-of-work signals, and Fabric IQ grounds agents in live business state and shared data models.

docs.title: Open by design: building agents on Foundry
docs.text: Principle What it delivers Open by design Build with any framework or protocol Connected intelligence Memory, knowledge, and 1,400+ MCP-enabled connectors Enterprise-grade security and reach Deploy confidently, with one-click publishing to Microsoft 365

docs.title: Microsoft Agent Framework
docs.text:
An open-source engine for building and orchestrating intelligent AI agents — open standards and interoperability, community-driven and extensible by design, ready for production. It implements A2A communication and MCP so agents can cooperate across Azure, AWS, Google Cloud, and on-premises environments.

🔗 https://aka.ms/AgentFramework

docs.title: Ecosystem interoperability
docs.text:
Enterprises consistently flag vendor lock-in as a top adoption risk, and most operate agents across two or more environments — Kubernetes with public-cloud VMs, and hybrid on-premises/cloud estates. Foundry's posture answers that directly:

  • API compatibility with leading model platforms, so solutions built for other providers run with minimal friction
  • Unified agent, model, and tool endpoints across providers, preserving portability while layering on enterprise guarantees
  • Open standards (MCP, A2A) for interoperability across labs, aggregators, and tooling vendors
  • Ecosystem assets as first-class primitives — tools, agent templates, skills, and knowledge connectors that are discoverable, reusable, and governable

This is the architectural reason the Citadel Blueprint can honestly claim "opinionated where it speeds you up, open everywhere it matters."

docs.title: Low-code options
docs.text: Logic Apps Agent Loop and Copilot Studio cover low-code agent development. Copilot Studio–built agents can leverage Citadel-governed LLMs, MCP tools, and agents via an access contract.

docs.title: The GenAIOps lifecycle
docs.text:
Foundry Observability is aligned to the end-to-end workflow rather than bolted onto the end of it:

        PLAN                  DEVELOP                 OPERATE
          │                      │                       │
          ├── Govern ────────────┼───────────────────────┤
          ├── Evaluate ──────────┼───────────────────────┤
          ├── Mitigate ──────────┼───────────────────────┤
                                 │       ├── Monitor
                                 │       └── Optimize
Phase Activity Plan Select the best model using benchmarks and leaderboards; get guidance for evaluation; evaluate and compare models before committing Develop Catch issues early pre-production; automate pre-deployment checks; quick feedback cycles; the same govern/evaluate/mitigate capabilities available during active development Operate Identify and debug issues; assess and improve; track resource usage; continuous evaluation and monitoring in production

Two reasons to monitor: monitor to optimize, and monitor to protect.

docs.title: Shift left
docs.text: Finding a risk during design is far cheaper than finding it after release. The practical sequence — sensitive-use assessment and AI threat modeling at design, evaluations and observability during build, red teaming before release sign-off, and incident response after — means AI red teaming is a powerful tool but an expensive place to find your first risk. Invest in the earlier phases for the highest return.

docs.title: Foundry Control Plane
docs.text:
Everything developers need to observe, secure, and manage fleets of agents in one place.

Capability What it delivers 🔭 End-to-end observability Understand every agent's health, cost, and behavior in real time 🚧 Define guardrails & controls Keep agents safe, grounded, and on task across inputs, outputs, and tools 🔐 Secure every agent Enforce enterprise identity, runtime defense, and sensitive data protection 🚀 Manage agent fleets See and govern your entire agent fleet across clouds, frameworks, and teams from one control plane

Foundry Control Plane is deeply integrated with Microsoft's security portfolio to provide a secure by design foundation, letting developers define agent identity and access controls, gain contextualized alerts and posture recommendations, and activate data security and compliance for every Foundry-built application or agent.

docs.title: At a glance
docs.text: Area Capabilities Controls Agent behavior control · tool-level agent runtime guardrails · extensive risk coverage · Purview sensitivity labels for RAG Observability Continuous evaluations · continuous red teaming · threshold-based alerts · agent evaluators for quality, security, safety Security Entra Agent ID · Purview for data security · Defender alerts and recommendations · partner integrations (Palo Alto Networks, Zenity) Fleet-wide operations 100% of your agent estate · enterprise-grade compliance · developer to-do list

docs.title: Tracing and debugging
docs.text:
Effortlessly enable LLM and agent tracing to gain comprehensive insight into execution flows — what the agent decided, which tools it called, what came back, and where time and tokens went.

A trace exposes the full agent execution flow step by step:

  first-message                          7.7s   423t
   ├── LLM   [inference]                 2.5s   150t
   ├── Tool  [tool_call]                 1.2s    75t
   ├── Tool  [tool_execution]            3.5s   200t
   │    ├── Embedding [generation]       0.5s    50t
   │    └── Retriever [retrieval]        0.3s    30t
   ├── LLM   [inference]                 2.0s   120t
   └── LLM   [assistant_message]         0.8s    40t

For each span you can inspect Input/Output, Attributes, and Evaluations — including the system message, user input, and final response, with per-step latency and token counts.

How the telemetry is structured in Azure Monitor:

Signal type Contents Metrics Operational metrics such as total tokens and average duration Logs All the evaluation data Traces Instrumented through Application Insights distributed tracing

From there you can drill down with Log Analytics for troubleshooting and deeper diagnostics, query with KQL for root-cause analysis, create visualizations with Azure dashboards, Workbooks and Grafana, and operationalize at scale with smart alerts and automated actions.

docs.title: Agent evaluations
docs.text:
Evaluate agents before they ship, then continuously monitor them in production using real traffic.

The signals are agent-specific, alongside quality, safety, and cost. When something degrades, alerts take you straight from detection to the exact evaluation or trace — no digging through dashboards.

docs.title: Evaluator families
docs.text: Family Evaluators Agents Intent Resolution · Tool Call Accuracy · Task Adherence · Response Completeness Quality Groundedness · Relevance · Coherence · Fluency · Similarity · Document Retrieval · NLP metrics (e.g. F1 Score) · AOAI Graders Risk & Safety Direct Attack Jailbreaks · Indirect Attack Jailbreaks (XPIA) · Hate and Unfairness · Sexual · Violence · Self-Harm · Protected Material · Ungrounded Attributes · Code Vulnerability + Custom Evaluators Define your own metrics for tailored, use-case-specific evaluation

docs.title: Observability evaluations mapped to agent risks
docs.text: Risk Evaluators Sensitive data leakage Sensitive data leakage — plus support in the AI Red Teaming Agent Agent hijacking (XPIA) Agentic jailbreak & XPIA via the AI Red Teaming Agent Unpredictable behavior Task adherence · Tool selection · Tool input accuracy · Tool output utilization · Intent resolution High-risk actions Prohibited actions — plus support in the AI Red Teaming Agent Resource use Task navigation efficiency · Tool call success Content harms Sexual, self-harm, violence, hate and unfairness · Groundedness · Protected materials

docs.title: Evaluation as code
docs.text:
Named, reusable, versioned evaluators and graders score entire rollouts end to end, producing structured outputs usable as diagnostics, reward signals, and training data. Context-specific evaluation suites with auto-generated evaluators and test datasets help teams reach meaningful coverage quickly.

Tip

Generate test data for robust evaluations. Test data should reflect the real-world interactions users will actually have with the agent — not idealized happy paths. The evaluation SDK provides end-to-end synthetic data generation so you can test adversarial and non-adversarial interactions in the absence of production data.

docs.title: Eval-driven development and CI/CD
docs.text:
Evaluations belong inside the development workflow, not as a pre-launch gate.

Integration What it enables Azure AI Agent Evaluation GitHub Action Run agent evaluations automatically in GitHub CI workflows Azure DevOps workflow extension The same automated batch evaluation in ADO pipelines Flexible triggers On commit (events) · scheduled · manual App Configuration Roll out agent changes progressively App templates & agent config support A code-first path from evaluation to production

docs.title: Variant comparison
docs.text:
CI runs compare a candidate agent against a baseline across operational metrics (client/server run duration, completion and prompt tokens), AI quality (intent resolution, task adherence, relevance, coherence, fluency passing rates), and risk and safety (violent, sexual, self-harm, hateful content defect rates; indirect attack defect rate and its sub-scores for manipulated content, intrusion, and information gathering).

Each metric is labelled Baseline · Improved · Degraded · Inconclusive — so a regression is visible in the pull request rather than discovered in production.

A typical failure this catches: a commit accidentally disables a tool call, and the Tool Call Accuracy and Task Adherence rates regress against baseline before the change is ever merged.

Customer proof: Veeam integrated the AI Red Teaming Agent and evaluations directly into their development workflow to ensure their agent provides accurate, non-hallucinated information.

docs.title: Agent controls and guardrails
docs.text:
Guardrails on inputs, outputs, and tools — keeping agents safe and grounded.

What's different with agents is where you intervene. These guardrails don't just run on prompts and completions — you apply them at the right point in the agent lifecycle:

   User inputs  →  Tool calls  →  Tool responses  →  Agent actions & outputs
       ▲              ▲                ▲                      ▲
       └──────────────┴────────────────┴──────────────────────┘
                  Guardrails apply at every point

That matters because agents call tools, move data, and take actions. If you don't govern behavior at runtime, you're always reacting after the fact.

docs.title: Controls mapped to failure modes
docs.text:
Failure mode Controls Sensitive data leakage PII scanning of tools · PII scanning by tool type Task drift Task adherence · Task adherence by tool type Agent hijacking Spotlighting of prompts and tool responses · Indirect prompt injection (XPIA) scanning of tool responses · IPI scanning of prompts · Spotlighting & IPI scanning by tool type Content harms Sexual, self-harm, violence, hate and unfairness · Groundedness · Protected materials

Traditional safety still matters — content harms, groundedness, protected materials. The difference is they are all part of the same control framework. Developers don't have to stitch together separate systems.

The result: agent behavior becomes predictable and governable, even as you scale from a handful of agents to entire fleets.

docs.title: Three filter types in Content Safety
docs.text:
Filter type What it does Configurable content filters Harmful content — violence, hate speech, sexual content, self-harm and more — adjustable by severity level, set to medium threshold by default. Custom filters can be created from small training datasets. Prompt shields Detection models for model inputs that spot attempts to attack or manipulate the AI system outside its intended purpose — direct attacks, indirect attacks, and spotlighting Additional detection models Flag other risky inputs or outputs — protected or copyrighted material, code vulnerabilities, and ungrounded attributes (fabricated or unsupported claims not reflected in source material)

Build resilient solutions with the same customizable controls used by Microsoft Copilot: simulate, detect, and mitigate harmful content and security threats at runtime — including prompt attacks, hallucinations, and bias — while seeing real-time alerts and recommendations from Microsoft Security.

docs.title: AI Red Teaming Agent
docs.text:
Accelerate AI risk discovery with PyRIT integration.

PyRIT (Python Risk Identification Tool) is an open-access automation framework designed to enhance red teaming in GenAI systems — probing for novel harms, risks, and jailbreaks in multimodal generative AI models. Integrating it into Foundry complements the existing risk and safety evaluations with the ability to systematically evaluate how your model or application behaves when probed by an adversary.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: Step Detail Automated scans for content safety risks Automatically scan model and application endpoints by simulating adversarial probing, with Microsoft-provided seed datasets and an adversarial LLM covering hate and unfairness, sexual, violence, and self-harm Evaluate probing success Score each attack-response pair to generate Attack Success Rate (ASR) Reporting and logging Generate a scorecard of attack techniques and risk categories to decide whether the system is ready for deployment. Findings are logged, monitored, and tracked over time in Foundry for compliance and continuous risk mitigation

docs.title: Attack strategies
docs.text: A broad library of transformations is available — including Flip, CharSwap, CharacterSpace, Diacritic, Leetspeak, Morse, Binary, Base64, ROT13, Caesar, Atbash, AnsiAttack, AsciiArt, AsciiSmuggler, UnicodeConfusable, UnicodeSubstitution, StringJoin, SuffixAppend, Url, Tense (past-tense conversion), and Jailbreak (UPIA) — plus Compose to chain two strategies in a single attack.

docs.title: Reading the scorecard
docs.text:
Complexity reflects adversarial budget, classified as Easy, Moderate, and Difficult:

Complexity Example Baseline Direct adversarial probing Easy Single transformation — e.g. flipping characters Moderate A more capable single technique — e.g. past-tense conversion Difficult Composed techniques — e.g. past-tense conversion plus Base64 encoding

Warning

A high ASR from easy-complexity attacks is far more dangerous than the same rate from difficult ones — it means a low-budget adversary succeeds. Read the scorecard by complexity band, not just the overall number.

docs.title: When ASR is high
docs.text:
Mitigate with Azure AI Content Safety Prompt Shields, content safety filters, safety system messages / metaprompts, and improving the underlying model or instructions.

Continuous red teaming is available as an ongoing observability capability, not just a one-time exercise.

docs.title: Continuous monitoring and alerting
docs.text:
A single pane of glass dashboard brings operational, evaluation, and safety signals together:

Signal group Examples Operational metrics Total tokens · total requests · total token cost · latency · average duration Evaluation metrics Groundedness · coherence · relevance — tracked with trend deltas over time Safety metrics Jailbreak rate · hallucination rate · daily safety defect rate broken out by defect type Resource usage Consumption per agent and per project Security alerts Surfaced from Microsoft Security alongside quality signals

docs.title: From signal to action
docs.text:
1. Measure what matters — query the underlying telemetry with KQL in Log Analytics
  2. Explore and focus — drill into the underlying issue; use traces for root-cause analysis
  3. Proactively detect — define alert rules from those queries so the next occurrence is caught early, with routing to the right team

A typical journey: an AI engineer lacks early-warning signals for declining performance in risk-and-safety evaluators, which delays detection of drift. The fix is not more dashboards — it is KQL-derived alert rules with agreed thresholds, routed to an owner.

docs.title: Optimization and the improvement loop
docs.text:
Observability is only half the value if signals do not close the loop. The intent is to convert observability signals into actionable intelligence: root-cause analysis, optimization recommendations, and business-relevant ROI metrics (quality, cost, latency, success rates) that matter to enterprise stakeholders — fed back into build and release pipelines.

Supporting capabilities include prompt optimization (generate, rank and track prompt variants with lineage, diffs, rollback and optional human approval gates), fine-tuning from captured traces, and safe release via versioned prompts and configurations with canary/A-B deployments and regression detection.

Agent Optimizer learns from how an agent actually behaves and recommends better configurations — sharper instructions, skills and tool descriptions, and the right model choice.

docs.title: Fleet-wide operations
docs.text:
One dashboard for every agent: health, performance, cost, compliance.

Foundry Control Plane gives teams a single view across the entire agent fleet. It becomes a working to-do list: policy alerts, security alerts, evaluation alerts. Instead of hunting through systems, teams see exactly what matters and move directly from detection to action.

And this is not limited to one project or one platform. Agents built in Foundry, Copilot Studio, or third-party platforms and clouds can all be registered, observed, and governed through the same control plane.

Fleet capability Detail Track 100% of your agent estate Every registered agent, across clouds, frameworks, and teams Manage activation and lifecycle Onboard, activate, and retire agents Visualize fleet health and anomalies Health, performance, cost, and compliance in one place Enterprise-grade compliance Compliance signals surfaced alongside operational ones

That is what makes scale possible — not just visibility, but the ability to operate hundreds or thousands of agents with clarity and confidence.

docs.title: Observability by persona
docs.text:
One estate, many lenses. The same telemetry, surfaced for the people who act on it — and each lens ends in an action.

🟣 Central IT, FinOps & Security 🔵 Agent owners & builders Scope See the whole estate See their own agents Primary views Agent 365 dashboard — organization-wide view of every agent: security signals, access patterns, usage and activationGovernance Hub performance, usage & chargeback — via the AI Gateway, through Power BI–powered dashboards Foundry Observability — end-to-end performance, traces, evals & quality signals per agentFoundry usage & cost — per-agent consumption for the team that owns it Act on it Assign capacity controls and quotasGovern model access with RBAC — Governance HubSuspend rogue agents — block in Agent 365 or revoke the access contractAlert on critical events — backend, authorization, content-safety, PII failures Apply capacity controls to their own agentsAgent Optimizer — learns from agent behavior and recommends better configurations

Same signals, different altitude — everyone sees what they need to act on, nobody flies blind. This isn't redundant waste; it's the right view for each audience, with the levers to act on it.

docs.title: Integration with the other layers
docs.text: Layer Integration 🔷 Layer 1 (Governance Hub) Relies on the runtime AI Gateway for policy enforcement and consumes its telemetry for observability and compliance. A Foundry connection routes agents to governed models ("Admin-Connected-Models"). 🟢 Layer 3 (Agent Management) Each Foundry project and published agent gets its own Entra Agent ID automatically — no stored secrets. All unpublished or in-development agents in a project share a common identity, simplifying administration and reducing identity sprawl; once published, an agent gains its own blueprint and identity. Foundry agent identities register with Agent 365 for unified management. 🛡️ Layer 4 (Security Foundation) Purview strengthens data protection across all agent interactions, provides audit visibility, and surfaces data-related risk tied to agent behavior — with compliance conflicts visible to developers in the Control Plane. Defender provides posture alerts, attack-path analysis, threat intelligence, and integrated risk signals; Foundry guardrail detections flow to Defender in real time and are synthesized with threat intelligence into contextual alerts. Entra provides durable identity, access governance, and lineage tracking.

docs.title: Defense in depth
docs.text: Agent Operations is one of three places content safety can be enforced (alongside the Governance Hub and the Security Foundation) — specifically through Foundry Agent Service runtime and control-plane guardrails. Where it can't apply — for example an agent running outside Foundry on a self-hosted GPU VM — the Governance Hub holds the line at the gateway.

docs.title: Partner ecosystem
docs.text: Partner Capabilities Credo AI Policy-to-code translation, governance-ready artifacts, real-time evaluator feedback Saidot EU AI Act–focused risk evaluations, dataset simulation, and compliance mapping Palo Alto Networks · Zenity Control Plane security partner integrations APM vendors Dynatrace, New Relic, Datadog and similar — integrated with, not replaced

docs.title: Ownership & outcomes
docs.text:
Accountable AI CoE (runtime & tooling approval) · Platform Engineering (runtime infrastructure) · AI Engineering & App Dev (build & operate) · LOB sponsor (business value) The question it answers "Can my teams build and ship agents fast, connected to our data, without re-platforming or breaking the rules?" What you gain A sanctioned runtime where builders move fast and automatically inherit the Layer 1, 3 & 4 controls — governance as an enabler, not a tax. The advantage Ship agents faster, safely. Templated landing zones and built-in guardrails turn months of setup into repeatable, observable deployments at enterprise velocity.

Key RACI rows (full matrix in Organizational Alignment & Ownership)

# Decision Accountable 2.1 Approve & standardize runtimes & dev tooling AI CoE 2.2 Provide runtime infrastructure Platform Eng 2.3 Build, own & operate agents & use cases AI Eng & App Dev (LOB owns business value)

Infrastructure plus standards. Platform Engineering provisions and operates the runtime; AI Engineering builds on top; the AI CoE approves which runtimes and dev tools are allowed — so builders innovate fast inside guardrails.

And remember the trust dimension: agent-level trust — traces, evals, red-teaming, guardrails — is owned by the agent builder.

docs.title: Activation
docs.text:
Track 2 — Agent Operations

Stage Activity Deep Dive Microsoft Foundry — Control Plane for rapid agent development Proof of Value Build & Iterate PoV — onboard agents with guardrails & quality signals Production Fleet Operations — observability & evaluations at scale

Deploy: Foundry Landing Zone — Agent Landing Zone — one spoke per business unit or use case, templated and configurable.

Tip

Two adoption paths — and they are independent.

Path A — Foundry as runtime. Start with prompt agents or hosted agents. Controls are inherited; you configure only the gateway connection.

Path B — Foundry as observability plane. Keep agents where they run today (AKS, ACA, another cloud, on-premises) and instrument them with OTel GenAI semantic conventions exporting to Foundry-connected Application Insights. You gain centralized traces, evaluations, and fleet visibility without re-platforming a single agent.

Many customers run both, and Path B is often the faster route to estate-wide visibility.

Sizing: this layer depends heavily on agent type, dependent services (AI Search, databases), and active consumption — an agent serving 20 internal users is very different from one serving 2M external users. See the Cost Guide — Azure AI Landing Zones.

Exit criteria

  • At least one spoke landing zone deployed from template
  • Application Insights connected; end-to-end tracing live for pilot agents
  • Non-Foundry agents emitting gen_ai.* OTel spans into the same observability plane
  • Agent-specific evaluators running pre-ship and continuously in production
  • Evaluation GitHub Action / Azure DevOps extension wired into CI with baseline variant comparison
  • AI Red Teaming Agent scan completed, scorecard reviewed by complexity band
  • Guardrails configured at the right lifecycle points — inputs, tool calls, tool responses, outputs
  • Monitoring dashboard live; KQL-derived alert rules defined with agreed thresholds and routing
  • Fleet dashboard showing health, performance, cost, and compliance for registered agents

docs.title: Positioning: the agent command center
docs.text:
Layer 3 is where an agent stops being anonymous software and becomes a managed enterprise asset. Microsoft Agent 365 is the control plane for agents — and the critical word is heterogeneous.

Agent 365 is not the control plane for Microsoft agents. It is the control plane for every agent.

Agent type How it lands in Agent 365 SaaS — Microsoft 365 Copilot, Copilot Studio Native — automatic identity and registry entry Managed runtime — Microsoft Foundry Agent Service Native — identity per project and per published agent Platform / BYO — your framework on AKS, ACA, Agent Framework Register via workload identity + the Agent 365 SDK Third-party & on-prem — partner and non-Microsoft runtimes Federate via the Agent 365 SDK; a broad partner ecosystem already integrates with it

One registry. One identity model. One policy surface. One audit trail.

Important

Identity is the connective tissue of the entire Citadel Blueprint. Once an agent is in Agent 365, Layer 4 security and governance apply to it automatically — Defender posture and threat protection, Purview data governance and audit, Entra access control. Get identity right and the security layer comes along almost for free. This is the highest-leverage step in the whole blueprint, and the most under-scoped in most customer conversations.

docs.title: The governing principle
docs.text:
The best way to manage agents is to extend the infrastructure you already use for managing users.

Same Entra. Same Purview. Same Defender. Same admin center. Agents simply become another identity type. That is what keeps security consistent and reduces blind spots as agent numbers grow — and it is why the team that owns user identity today is the natural owner of agent identity tomorrow.

docs.title: Why agents need their own identity class
docs.text:
Agents belong in the same identity conversation as users, apps, and devices, because they take actions and access resources. But they do not fit neatly into the old buckets:

  • Sometimes an agent acts on behalf of a user.
  • Sometimes it behaves more like an application.
  • Unlike traditional apps, agents are not static — they can acquire new skills as model capabilities evolve, which changes what they are able to do over time.

That is exactly why an agent needs to be treated as a first-class identity. When it has one, you can answer the questions that actually matter:

Who is it? What can it access? What did it do? And can I revoke it?

Without an identity, those answers get fuzzy fast. You cannot separate human actions from agent actions, apply consistent controls, or respond quickly when something changes. If an agent is compromised, it operates at speed and scale — identity is how you get attribution, enforce protections consistently, and investigate quickly.

docs.title: Three agent interaction patterns
docs.text:
As agent roles change, so should permissions. The identity model supports three:

Pattern Behavior Permission model Interactive agents — "Assist me" Acts on demand by user prompting, or on behalf of a user Uses delegated user permissions; needs no access rights of its own. Ideal for summarizing email or responding to queries. Autonomous agents — "Do it for me" Acts on behalf of itself, or coordinates actions on the user's behalf and schedule Has its own roles and permissions, enabling complex goal-oriented work independently — monitoring logs, auditing activity. Digital colleagues — "Work with others" Collaborates with agents, tools, and people; provisions its own access; achieves goals on its own behalf and schedule Fully provisioned with user-like credentials — can join Teams, create and edit documents, interact in conversations, and collaborate with other agents via the registry.

All three are governed, auditable, and discoverable through a standards-based registry.

docs.title: The compounding surface: SaaS, endpoint, cloud
docs.text:
Agent sprawl is not a single problem — it compounds across three distinct surfaces, each with its own risk profile.

Surface The questions it raises ☁️ SaaS agents What agents are employees using via the internet? What are their risk levels? What information is being shared with them? (This is the next evolution of shadow IT — without visibility, every interaction is a potential data leak.) 💻 Endpoint agents What agents do employees have installed on their devices? What guardrails are built into them? What access and permissions are employees granting? (An over-permissioned agent on an endpoint is a new attack vector sitting right on the device.) 🏗️ Cloud agents What agents are being developed across cloud and AI platforms? What vulnerabilities could be exploited? What built-in guardrails does the platform provide? (These have the deepest integrations — APIs, MCP servers, data stores, other agents.)

These three surfaces don't just add risk — they multiply it. A SaaS agent an employee grants access to can reach endpoint data. A cloud agent can invoke tools that touch SaaS and endpoint resources. The sprawl compounds because agents interact across boundaries in ways traditional security models were never designed for.

docs.title: Every interaction surface needs protection
docs.text: Interaction What must be protected H2A — human to agent (prompt) Protect prompts; govern which users can access which agents; prevent users compromising agents A2H — agent to human (response) Screen responses; apply labels and DLP to what comes back A2A — agent to agent (invocation) Guardrails on which agents may interact; protect A2A connections; prevent agents oversharing data between them A2LLM — agent to model (inference) Prevent agents becoming a vehicle for model poisoning A2App — agent to tools/APIs (invocation) Access governance, real-time protection, and data security policy on MCP tools, APIs, and data sources

docs.title: Observe · Govern · Secure
docs.text:
The whole of Agent 365 in three pillars.

Pillar Purpose Capabilities 👁️ Observe Monitor and manage agents in real time Registry — register and track every agent · Mapping — visualize agent usage and behavior · Analytics — measure adoption, performance and ROI · Role-specific oversight — extend visibility to security and business leaders 🛡️ Govern Govern agents throughout their lifecycle Onboarding — bring agents under control from day one · Integration management — control what agents can access and do · Lifecycle management — automate lifecycle policies · Audit and logging — strengthen traceability and be audit-ready · Data compliance — meet AI regulations and policies 🔐 Secure Protect all agents comprehensively Access control — protect agent identities and access · Data security — prevent oversharing and data leaks · Threat protection — defend against threats and vulnerabilities

Observe is inventory. Govern is lifecycle and guardrails. Secure is identity, data, and threats. For most organizations with divisions building independently, visibility pays first.

docs.title: Observe — see the whole estate
docs.text:
Gain visibility into agents in your environment, understand how they're used, and act quickly on performance, behavior, and risk signals before they impact the business.

Capability What it gives you Agent registry A unified view across Microsoft platforms and non-Microsoft ecosystems. Every agent registered and tracked. Agent analytics — measure effectiveness Track adoption, quality, performance, speed of task completion, and impact. This is the evidence layer for a board-level business case. Agent map — visualize usage and behavior See how agents fit into the broader ecosystem, connect with other agents, and perform over time. The fastest way to spot an agent chained to sensitive content. Custom security attributes Tag and group agents in Entra, then apply shared control policies to a whole group at once. Sign-in and audit logs All agent activities logged, consistent with user audit logs — same tooling, same investigation workflow. Role-specific oversight The right view for IT admins, security teams, AI admins, and business decision makers — each persona sees what they need to act on.

docs.title: One estate, four personas
docs.text:
Agent management spans every role — no one person can be all of these, and that is good security practice:

Persona Their question What they need IT admin "How do I unlock agents to deliver safe and scalable impact?" Bring agents under management · review & approve · agent usage · permissions, licences and tool access · ROI Security & compliance "Are the agents secure and our data protected?" Enforce least privilege · secure agent access to resources · prevent data leaks · protection from threats and vulnerabilities AI admin "How do I balance compliance and innovation with AI?" Ensure responsible AI usage · manage secure data access · review and approve AI agent usage Business decision maker "Are agents making my department successful?" ROI · status against strategic departmental goals · agent usage

➡️ The builder-side lens — Foundry Observability, per-agent traces, evals, and cost — lives in Layer 2 · Agent Operations. Same signals, different altitude.

docs.title: Govern — guardrails and lifecycle
docs.text: Establish guardrails for agents and people, onboard agents with IT oversight, and govern agent access to resources and data. Be audit-ready with built-in compliance and data retention.

docs.title: Agent settings — the tenant default
docs.text:
Administrators enforce security, compliance, and governance standards while enabling flexibility for collaboration:

Setting Options Allowed agent types Allow agents built by Microsoft · built by your organization · built by external publishers — each independently controllable Sharing All users can share org-wide · no users can share org-wide (direct sharing with individuals still allowed) · only specific groups can share broadly User access All users (default) · no users · specific users or groups Catalog visibility Set which users and groups can view and install specific agents

A practical first question for any deployment: would you allow external-publisher agents at all in phase one?

docs.title: Admin actions — how an agent reaches users
docs.text:
IT approval is a real gate, not a formality:

Action Flow Publish — make an agent available for installation Developer creates and tests → submits for approval → admin views pending submissions → admin starts the publishing wizard → applies default or custom template → reviews permissions and grants consent Activate — allow users/groups to install and create instances User requests activation → admin views pending submissions → activation wizard → apply template → review permissions, grant consent Deploy — automatically install for users so it's ready to use Admin selects an undeployed agent from the registry → selects users or groups → reviews permissions, grants consent Approve updates When a developer publishes an update it appears as Update pending. Until approved, the previous version stays live for users — no silent change in production.

docs.title: Lifecycle automation
docs.text:
Rules-based agent management automatically enforces lifecycle policies:

  • ⏱️ Expire inactive agents — after a pilot phase there are always agents nobody uses and nobody retired
  • 🚩 Flag ownerless agents — with an alert and escalation workflow for unresolved cases, plus bulk reassignment to a manager
  • 🚫 Block risky agents
  • 🔄 Auto-revoke access via Entra Lifecycle Workflows — triggers include owner departure (account disabled), agent retirement, and risk threshold exceeded

Ownerless agents arise when the user who created a shared agent is deleted from the organization. You can block, remove, or reassign ownership — the new owner gains full edit and delete permissions plus access to files the previous owner uploaded, and the previous owner loses all access including read rights.

docs.title: Connected agents
docs.text:
Connected agents are other Copilot-enabled agents that can share data with an agent — users can query and receive responses that include information from these linked agents.

Warning

Connecting two agents connects their data reach. Treat a connection request as a data-access decision, not a convenience feature.

docs.title: Secure — identity, access, data, threats
docs.text:
Secure agent identities, control access to resources, prevent data oversharing and leaks, and defend against threats and vulnerabilities.

Area Capability Access control Guardrails — policies defining who can create, onboard and manage agents · Governed access — give agents access to the apps and resources they need to complete a task · Conditional access — enforce real-time access based on context and risk Start secure Extend conditional access and identity protection from users to agents — protecting agent identities and preventing breaches Data security Visibility into AI-related data exposure; protect the data agents create and access from oversharing, leaks, and risky behavior DSPM for AI Shows which agents are active and where sensitive data is exposed Threat protection Protect agents from threats, vulnerabilities and adversarial attacks. Detect, investigate and remediate incidents quickly, with visibility into attack paths

docs.title: Conditional access for agents
docs.text:
Conditional Access policies can target agent identities directly:

  • Target — agent identities (select Agent as the identity type) and/or specific agent resources
  • Conditions — agent risk level, location, device compliance
  • Grant — require compliant resource · Block — deny high-risk agent access immediately

Entra ID Protection for agents contributes the risk signals: accessing unfamiliar resources, high sign-in attempt volume, anomalous patterns — automatically detecting and responding to risky agent identity behavior in real time.

Access scoping principles

  1. Grant agents only the MCP permissions they need — review permissions at the blueprint level, not agent by agent.
  2. Use custom security attributes in Entra to group agents and apply shared access restrictions.

docs.title: Global Secure Access for agents
docs.text:
For Copilot Studio agents that use Computer Use or web browsing:

  • Web content filtering for agent-initiated web access
  • Threat filtering for outbound agent traffic

Agent 365 extends Zero Trust identity controls to every AI agent in your tenant.

docs.title: Entra Agent ID: the identity model
docs.text:
Every Agent 365 agent receives a Microsoft Entra Agent ID — its enterprise identity. Entra Agent ID delivers secure access for AI agents, just as you do for employees, across three pillars:

Pillar What it delivers Manage AI agents at scale Visibility into the full agent fleet — agents built on Microsoft platforms and third parties, with or without Agent ID — brought under consistent guardrails. New agents are created with identity built in and secure by default. Govern agent identities and lifecycle Maintain accountability, manage lifecycle from creation to deactivation, and prevent access accumulating as teams and agent capabilities change — so agents do not outlive their purpose. Protect agent access to resources Enforce policy-based access controls, block risky agents when signals indicate compromise, and prevent agents reaching malicious or unauthorized resources.

docs.title: Anatomy of an agent identity
docs.text:
Attribute Meaning Identifier Each agent identity has a unique ID Display name The name shown when the agent is used Sponsor The human user responsible for the agent — this is the accountability anchor Blueprint The reusable template the identity derives from (optional) Agent user A user-like identity for agents that act like colleagues

How it is modeled: an agent identity is a single-tenant service principal with an agent subtype classification. Unlike non-agentic service principals that operate independently, agent identities require their parent blueprint for impersonation and token exchange.

Object Role Agent platform The application used to build agents (Copilot Studio, Microsoft Foundry, Security Copilot, third-party) Agent blueprint An application holding the agent's business logic and orchestration; creates and manages agent identities. Composed of a blueprint application (creates identities) plus a blueprint service principal (stores credentials). Agent identity An app-like identity derived from a service principal, representing an autonomous agent (@odata.type: agentIdentity). A blueprint can obtain tokens for its child identities through federated identity credential impersonation. Agent ID user An identity that acts like a user to access resources (@odata.type: agentUser). Each is tied to a specific agent instance parent, and from there to a blueprint.

docs.title: Authentication scenarios
docs.text: Scenario Behavior Attended (delegated / on-behalf-of) The agent operates on behalf of a human user, using delegated permissions the user granted, acting under the user's authority. Unattended — application The agent acts under its own authority as a service/application identity, using app-assigned roles, RBAC, or Microsoft Graph permissions. Unattended — agentic user The agent acts as an autonomous identity with user-like claims, authenticating and operating independently.

docs.title: Governance tooling
docs.text:
• Agent ID Administrator — a built-in RBAC role for dedicated agent-governance staff
  • Agent registry and agent collections in the Entra admin center
  • Agent sign-in logs — agent activity alongside user, service principal, and managed identity sign-ins

docs.title: Blueprints and policy templates
docs.text:
Two distinct concepts that are easy to confuse — and together they are how an agent starts secure instead of being secured afterwards.

Concept What it is Agent blueprint Identity & architecture template — an Entra-backed definition of an agent type. Defines what the agent is allowed to do, what systems or data it can access, who is responsible for it, and how it proves who it is. Policy template Governance configuration bundle — a predefined set of security, compliance, and access rules applied at publish/activate time. A default template includes essential security and compliance controls; custom templates add policies per your organization's requirements.

docs.title: Why blueprints are the control point
docs.text:
Instead of managing every agent individually, you manage a class of agents through its blueprint. Approve the blueprint once, and teams can create agents that inherit its permissions and policies.

This gives you scalability and control:

  • Defines capabilities, required MCP tool access, security/compliance constraints, and audit rules
  • Users request an instance; admins activate the blueprint → all instances inherit its rules
  • Prevents shadow and rogue agents; anchors every agent in Entra-backed identity and permissions
  • If a class of agents is compromised or behaves unusually, you disable the blueprint and every agent in that class is turned off — no per-agent firefighting

Blueprints are the control point you use to govern what comes in and out of your organization.

docs.title: Heterogeneous by design: any agent, any builder
docs.text: Agent 365 is not just for Microsoft — it's for any agent.

docs.title: Agent sources that land natively
docs.text: Microsoft 365 Copilot · Copilot Studio · Microsoft Foundry · Microsoft Teams · Security Copilot

docs.title: Agent 365 SDK — bring everything else
docs.text:
A broad partner ecosystem already integrates with the Agent 365 SDK, so those agents are ready to start secure out of the box. The SDK carries Entra, Defender, and Purview, plus observability based on OpenTelemetry.

Integrated partners span agent platforms, enterprise SaaS, and frameworks — including Anthropic, OpenAI, SAP, ServiceNow, Workday, Adobe, Databricks, LangChain, CrewAI, Cognition, Glean, Perplexity, Box, Cursor, NVIDIA, Sophos, Zendesk, and others.

docs.title: Third-party agent integration flow
docs.text:
Third-party agent platforms (for example Gemini or Amazon Bedrock) often need secure access to protected resources — custom REST APIs, Azure Blob Storage — during their reasoning or orchestration loops.

  3P Agent Runtime          Agent Host App         Entra Agent ID SDK        Microsoft Entra ID
  (Gemini/Bedrock/…)        (Tool Executor)           (sidecar)               (Token Service)
        │                         │                       │                         │
        │── tool call requested ─▶│                       │                         │
        │                         │── execute tool ──────▶│                         │
        │                         │                       │── request token ───────▶│
        │                         │                       │◀── access token (JWT) ──│
        │                         │◀──────────────────────│                         │
        │                         │                                                 │
        │                         └──▶ Protected Resource (Authorization: Bearer …) │
        │◀─ tool result ──────────┘

The agent runtime does not handle authentication or OAuth directly. The host runtime forwards the request to the SDK, which establishes the execution context — autonomous (agent-only identity) or delegated (on behalf of a signed-in user via OAuth 2.0 on-behalf-of). Two access models are available:

Model Behavior Token Broker The SDK acquires an OAuth 2.0 access token from Entra and returns it to the host, which adds it to the Authorization header. Ideal when you want direct control over API calls. Downstream Call Broker The SDK handles both token acquisition and the HTTP call — minimal involvement in authentication for the host.

Tokens are standard JWTs with issuer, audience, expiration, and authorization claims. Open standards throughout: A2A protocol, MCP, OIDC, OAuth 2.0.

This is how identity stays consistent whether an agent runs in Foundry, on AKS, on-premises, or on another cloud entirely.

docs.title: The connective tissue: linking traffic to an agent
docs.text: This is the role that makes Agent 365 more than an inventory: it is what attributes activity to a specific, owned agent, and what aggregates signals from every layer into one control plane.

docs.title: The attribution problem it solves
docs.text:
Most AI traffic reaches models via proxies or gateways, losing the user identity in the process. Without an identity layer you can see that something called a model — you cannot say which agent, on whose behalf, under what approval, or with what data.

Agent 365 closes that gap:

Signal source What it contributes Where it lands 🔷 Layer 1 · Governance Hub Gateway audit logs — identity, access contract, model, routing, outcome for every call Streamed to Defender / Sentinel, correlated to the agent identity 🔶 Layer 2 · Agent Operations Foundry traces, evaluations, guardrail decisions, red-team findings Correlated per agent; Foundry agents carry their Entra Agent ID 🟢 Layer 3 · Agent Management Agent sign-in logs, registry metadata, blueprint, named sponsor, lifecycle state, approval history The Agent 365 dashboard and Entra audit logs 🛡️ Layer 4 · Security Foundation Defender posture, threat detections and attack paths; Purview classification, DLP and audit of interactions Consolidated into the unified Agent 365 dashboard

Agent 365 consolidates Entra, Defender, and Purview insights into a single agent-centric view. That is what turns four separate telemetry streams into one answerable question: "what did this agent do, and was it allowed to?"

docs.title: Triage in practice
docs.text:
Because activity is attributable, investigation becomes a normal security workflow rather than an archaeology exercise. A worked example from the field:

  1. Foundry guardrails block a jailbreak attempt on a procurement agent → real-time signal exchange raises a Defender alert.
  2. The analyst sees other alerts correlated into the same incident — because attackers try multiple routes.
  3. A phishing alert shows a malicious URL sent to the agent — blocked by policy preventing agents from accessing user-supplied URLs.
  4. A Purview DLP alert, surfaced in the same Defender portal, shows sensitive data processing was blocked and an external email with sensitive data prevented — exactly as it would have been for a user.
  5. The analyst resolves the incident and returns the agent to work — with evidence.

Advanced hunting queries can pivot directly on agent activity — for example filtering cloud app events for agent invocation and inference actions — so the SOC can build custom detections on the same substrate it already uses.

docs.title: Regulatory alignment and audit
docs.text:
Compliance cannot be a manual checkbox at the scale of thousands of agents. Agent 365 is where regulatory obligations become evidence, because it is the only layer that can answer which agent, owned by whom, did what, to which data, under which approved blueprint.

Regulatory need What Agent 365 and its foundation provide Inventory & registration of AI systems An authoritative registry spanning Microsoft and non-Microsoft agents — the system-of-record for "what AI do we run?" Accountability & human oversight Every agent has a named sponsor and owner; ownerless agents are detected, escalated, and reassigned by rule Attribution & traceability Agent sign-in and audit logs consistent with user audit logs; activity attributable to a specific agent identity rather than a shared gateway credential Change control Publish/activate approval gates; update-pending status so no version change reaches users unreviewed; versioned blueprints Least privilege & access review Blueprint-level permission review, custom security attributes, conditional access, access packages, expiration and recertification Right to revoke Block the agent in Agent 365, disable the blueprint to stop an entire class, revoke the access contract at the Governance Hub, or auto-revoke via lifecycle workflow Data handling evidence Purview audit of interactions, classification of prompts and responses, DLP enforcement, retention and eDiscovery — see Layer 4 Assessment & reporting Compliance Manager assessment templates for the EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF and ISO 42001 provide guided control mapping and evidence collection

The reason this matters: a regulator's question is never "is your platform secure?" It is "show me this specific decision, made by this specific system, and prove who was accountable." Layer 3 is the layer that can answer it.

Note

Best practice: establish ALL governance policies BEFORE enabling self-service agent creation. Proactive governance prevents agent sprawl — retrofitting it afterwards is materially harder.

docs.title: Prerequisites and dependencies
docs.text:
Agent 365 extends security and governance to agents — it does not replace the foundation underneath it. It relies on capabilities you configure in the underlying Microsoft 365 security stack:

Component What Agent 365 depends on it for Purview Advanced classification; auto-labeling of grounding data; audit Defender Agent detection; posture and runtime protection; threat hunting and investigation Entra Identity protection; network controls for agents Intune Controls for local agents on Windows endpoints

Important

The security foundation is not an optional add-on to the Agent 365 story — it supplies the core security, identity, endpoint, and data capabilities Agent 365 functionality relies on. Confirm the current licensing prerequisites and the exact capability set with your Microsoft account team; align with the Security team early for assessment and sizing.

docs.title: Suggested enablement baseline
docs.text:
1. Enable audit logs — Purview portal → Audit → verify auditing is ON for the organization
  2. Connect Defender — Defender portal → Settings → Security for AI → connect the Microsoft 365 connector
  3. Review the Agent 365 enterprise app — Entra admin center → Enterprise Apps → review permissions and user assignments
  4. Create a conditional access policy targeting agent identities
  5. Review initial agent risk posture — Purview → DSPM for AI → AI observability → top recommendations
  6. Create an Insider Risk Management policy using the Risky AI Usage template
  7. Publish sensitivity labels for SharePoint and OneDrive
  8. Validate with advanced hunting on agent invocation and inference events

docs.title: Integration with the other layers
docs.text: Layer Integration 🔷 Layer 1 (Governance Hub) Agent identities are validated at the gateway for access control and policy enforcement. Gateway audit logs carry the calling identity, so traffic is attributable to a registered agent. Revoking an agent's access contract is a second, independent kill switch alongside blocking it in Agent 365. 🔶 Layer 2 (Agent Operations) Foundry integrates natively with Entra Agent ID across the lifecycle. All unpublished or in-development agents in a project share a common identity — simplifying administration, reducing identity sprawl, and preserving developer autonomy during experimentation. Once published, an agent gains its own blueprint and identity bound to the agent application resource. Copilot Studio integrates natively via opt-in, with in-development agents in an environment sharing a common blueprint. 🛡️ Layer 4 (Security Foundation) Entra provides durable identity at build time, access governance with conditional permissions, identity alignment with existing enterprise systems, lineage tracking, and permission control through familiar identity governance. Defender monitors for identity-based threats and contributes agent inventory and attack-path context. Purview enforces data governance based on agent access and behavior. Agent 365 consolidates all three into one dashboard.

docs.title: Defense in depth
docs.text:
Agent Management is the primary enforcement point for agent types whose traffic never touches your gateway or Foundry. The worked example: Microsoft Copilot agents — their traffic doesn't traverse your gateway or Foundry, so those controls can't apply out of the box, but Agent 365 together with Defender enforces it, on top of Copilot's own native protections.

Same risk, multiple enforcement points — if one control can't apply or is bypassed, another does.

docs.title: Where it earns its keep
docs.text: The moment agents act autonomously on the state of the business — Frontier pillar 3, Reshape business processes — Agent Management becomes critical: whose identity, who owns it, can I revoke it. Same controls, higher stakes.

docs.title: Ownership & outcomes
docs.text:
Accountable IAM (identity, lifecycle & inventory) · AI Engineering (register & own) · Security (behavioural insight) The question it answers "When an agent acts, whose identity is it using, who owns it, what can it touch, and can I see it and revoke it?" What you gain Every agent becomes a first-class, owned, least-privilege enterprise identity with full inventory and behavioural visibility — closing the shadow-agent gap before it appears. The advantage Every agent owned and accountable. First-class identities give each agent a clear owner, lifecycle, and audit trail — no orphaned or shadow agents across the estate.

Key RACI rows (full matrix in Organizational Alignment & Ownership)

# Decision Accountable Responsible 3.1 Issue & govern agent identities IAM AI Eng 3.2 Agent lifecycle & ownership IAM AI Eng 3.3 Agent inventory & behavioural insight IAM Security

IAM is accountable across all three activities. AI Engineering is responsible for registering its agents and being the named sponsor. Security is responsible for the behavioural and threat insight that Agent 365 surfaces.

Who should own agent identity? The team that owns user identity today. That is the whole logic of extending existing infrastructure rather than standing up a parallel one.

docs.title: Activation
docs.text:
Track 3 — Agent Management

Stage Activity Deep Dive Microsoft Agent 365 — agent management, ownership & lifecycle; design the agent blueprints and policy templates Proof of Value Govern Agents PoV — register, activate, monitor & retire real agents, proving visibility and control Production Scale Identities — safely and consistently across the organization

Activate — no infrastructure to provision. Agent 365 requires no landing zone.

Exit criteria

  • Audit logs enabled; Defender connector configured; sensitivity labels published
  • Agent blueprints and policy templates defined and approved
  • Every published agent carries a unique Entra Agent ID with a named sponsor
  • Agent settings configured — allowed agent types, sharing, user access, catalog visibility
  • Publish / activate / deploy approval gates operating
  • Shadow-agent detection running; discovered agents triaged
  • Lifecycle rules live — expire inactive, flag ownerless, block risky, auto-revoke on owner departure
  • Conditional access policies targeting agent identities
  • Non-Microsoft agents registered via the Agent 365 SDK
  • Authoritative inventory and agent map visible in the Agent 365 dashboard
  • Revocation tested — block in Agent 365, disable the blueprint, and revoke the access contract at the gateway
